671.skill_name: Using the depression/Anxiety questionnaire for weekly mood assessment
671.skill_description: Using standard Anxiety/depression questionnaires to psychologically assess the past week's emotions, and repeating weekly, to quantify current severity and changes, as the main basis for Assessing mood and monitoring efficacy.
671.when_to_use: At the start of subsequent Consultative sessions, when needing to understand the severity of the client's psychological problems or post-counseling improvement, for efficacy monitoring.
671.trigger: When the client is about one week from the last session and entering the start phase, needing quantitative data on this week's Anxiety or depression level.

672.skill_name: Uses a 0-100 emotion scale to subjectively rate mood
672.skill_description: Guide the client to use a 0-100 percentage scale to subjectively rate the intensity of other emotions or the overall mood, obtaining concise quantitative data, assisting in grasping the current state and change trends.
672.when_to_use: When conducting mood assessment at the start phase, needing to understand the intensity of other emotions or overall mood besides Anxiety/depression.
672.trigger: The client talks about feelings regarding other emotions or overall mood, needing to convert their subjective experience into a quantifiable value.

673.skill_name: Compare weekly questionnaire results to assess counseling progress
673.skill_description: Longitudinally comparing the weekly scores of Anxiety/depression questionnaires, evaluating counseling progress based on the magnitude of improvement or deterioration, providing a basis for progress judgment in subsequent sessions.
673.when_to_use: After completing this week's assessment in the opening segment, changes compared with earlier results need to be judged to grasp the efficacy trend.
673.trigger: When two or more consecutive Anxiety/depression questionnaire results have been obtained, and the client's score this week shows improvement or deterioration compared to last week.

681.skill_name: Explain the purpose and routine of agenda setting
681.skill_description: Introduce to the client the meaning and routine nature of agenda setting / schedule setting, emphasize that it can raise efficiency and focus on the most concerned problems, and invite them to jointly participate in determining today's topics, establishing structured cooperation.
681.when_to_use: At the very start of the beginning phase, before formal discussion, needing to establish session structure and expectations, especially at the first or early Consultative sessions to enhance cooperation and focus.
681.trigger: When the client is unclear about the session process or says 'just chatting casually' or 'do not know what to talk about today', showing a lack of understanding of structure and goals.

682.skill_name: Proposing a preliminary session agenda outline
682.skill_description: After explaining the concepts, proactively give today's preliminary agenda list, briefly outline the main parts and process, as a structural reference for discussion, providing a framework for subsequent additions and choices.
682.when_to_use: At the opening segment, right after the agenda setting is introduced, the content of today's discussion needs to be concretized to make it easy for the client to understand and participate.
682.trigger: When the client is Silent about arrangements or responds 'anything is fine' or 'I will follow your lead', not yet actively proposing specific topics, needing the therapist to provide structure first.

683.skill_name: Inviting additional agenda items and explaining questions
683.skill_description: Asks the client with open questions what topic they hope to discuss today, includes their concerns in the agenda list; if they have questions about the agenda, gives a brief explanation to increase understanding and participation.
683.when_to_use: After the preliminary agenda is proposed, to ensure the agenda is centered on the client's needs, soliciting additions and confirmation before finalizing.
683.trigger: The client says 'I want to discuss...' or 'I have a question to ask', or expresses confusion about the agenda, raising questions such as 'why is it arranged this way?'.

684.skill_name: Judge based on recent information whether to include and limit details
684.skill_description: Ask the client to summarize the key events of the most recent week, assess whether they need to be included in the agenda; avoid overly detailed narration, leaving concrete discussion to the middle part to save time.
684.when_to_use: After obtaining the latest information in the opening component, when setting today's agenda it is necessary to decide which events enter the list and control discussion depth.
684.trigger: The client begins to unfold in detail the process and particulars of recent negative events, and the narration time lengthens, exceeding the degree of overview needed for agenda setting.

685.skill_name: Summarizing agenda sources and listing them
685.skill_description: Clarifying the scope of agenda sources: issues the client did not resolve last week or will encounter next week, counseling relationship or setting matters (such as Homework), last session's unfinished topics, organizing them uniformly into the list.
685.when_to_use: At the start of subsequent Consultative sessions, when setting the agenda, needing to comprehensively collect today's discussable topics, preventing omission of key matters.
685.trigger: When the client mentions last week's leftover issues, Anticipating next week's challenges, or expressing confusion about Homework and the counseling relationship, and recalling last session's unfinished topics.

686.skill_name: Determine priority topics from the list
686.skill_description: When the agenda is large, jointly select with the client from the list one topic with the highest priority, and limit the number discussed this time (one to two items), ensuring the session is focused and effective.
686.when_to_use: At the closing stage of the agenda setting in the start segment, needing to clarify the focus and discussion scope for this session to manage time.
686.trigger: The agenda list contains multiple items to discuss; the client hopes to discuss many issues or says 'there is a lot today', and priorities need to be jointly determined.

710.skill_name: Asking about and identifying this session's key gains
710.skill_description: In session feedback, invite the client to point out the most important gains in this session and record them. Judge from their answers whether the important content has been mastered, and when necessary plan to reinforce the relevant key points again in subsequent sessions.
710.when_to_use: When entering Session feedback at the Consultative session's ending phase, for reviewing and consolidating this session's discussion outcomes and preparing for subsequent arrangements.
710.trigger: When the session enters the feedback stage, needing to understand the client's gains; when the client has not yet actively summarized or describes gains vaguely.

711.skill_name: Assess the likelihood of homework completion and adjust assignment strategy
711.skill_description: In feedback, asking about Homework feasibility and difficulties, adjusting the assignment based on willingness level: abandoning the homework when willingness to complete is below 50%, setting it as optional when between 50% and 80%, and identifying hindering factors.
711.when_to_use: Before and after confirming the homework in the closing segment, assess the feasibility of homework execution through session feedback, ensuring the assignment matches the client's willingness.
711.trigger: When the client's willingness for Homework is unclear or expresses concerns and difficulties, needing to quantify completion possibility through feedback questions and identify obstacles.

712.skill_name: Exploring and handling discomfort and confusion in the session
712.skill_description: In feedback, directly asking whether this session had anything that made the client uncomfortable or confused, prompting them to express true feelings, and handling negative thoughts and emotions promptly, to maintain and consolidate the counseling relationship.
712.when_to_use: When the session is about to end and feedback is being conducted, the goal is maintaining the relationship, eliminating negative experiences, and preventing accumulated dissatisfaction from causing counseling dropout.
712.trigger: When the client expresses discomfort, confusion, or negative emotions in feedback, or appears dissatisfied and hesitant about the session process, needing timely response and handling.

713.skill_name: Collecting unresolved questions and incorporating them into subsequent agendas
713.skill_description: In feedback, asking whether there is anything else they want to clarify, collecting unresolved issues; if this session's time is insufficient, listing them in the next session's agenda, ensuring issues are subsequently discussed and resolved.
713.when_to_use: At the feedback stage of the ending phase, for organizing unresolved matters and planning topics for the next session.
713.trigger: When the client raises additional questions or reveals not yet clarified topics at the fourth feedback question stage, needing to record and arrange subsequent discussion.

687.skill_name: Guide a review of this session's topics and key points
687.skill_description: At the ending stage, invite the client and counselor to jointly review what problems were discussed today, sort out the topics handled and core key points, help clearly grasp this session's content, so as to strengthen the gains and effect of the session.
687.when_to_use: At the Consultative session's ending phase, when the current agenda discussion is complete, needing an overall review and integration of this session.
687.trigger: The client's narration comes to a pause or a pause awaiting summary appears, asking 'what did we talk about today?' or showing expressions and statements indicating a need to organize information.

688.skill_name: Inviting the client to state this session's takeaways
688.skill_description: In the summary, guide the client to state the gains from this session and the content important to themselves, expressing experiences and insights in their own language, so as to enhance mastery of the key points and raise the overall effect of the session.
688.when_to_use: At the session summary stage of the closing segment, after completing the review of topics and key points, when learning and gains need to be further consolidated.
688.trigger: When the client expresses evaluative statements like 'somewhat understand/limited gains', or shows confusion, expecting to be asked about gains and willing to summarize.

689.skill_name: Clarify and record key points worth noting
689.skill_description: Ask about and jointly determine the key points in this session that are 'worth writing down', prompting the client to record important content in their notes, deepening the impression and laying the groundwork for subsequent follow-up and homework.
689.when_to_use: During the summary at the closing stage or right after the review ends, to consolidate gains and prepare for follow-up work while avoiding forgetting key content.
689.trigger: The client expresses worry about forgetting or asks 'what do I need to write down?'; nods in recognition of certain points and takes out a notebook, showing willingness to record.

674.skill_name: Guide a brief review of events since last time
674.skill_description: Define the time range as 'from the last counseling to this session', openly invite the client to briefly outline the main events and changes that occurred in their life, obtain only outline clues, providing basic information for subsequent agenda selection and mid-session handling.
674.when_to_use: At the start of subsequent Consultative sessions, after completing mood assessment, entering the 'Obtaining the latest information' step, needing to quickly grasp the client's recent situation and locate potential topics.
674.trigger: When the client has not yet actively reported their recent situation or appears hesitant about how to start the review, with pauses in conversation, needing structured time framing and Questioning to start the review.

675.skill_description: After Listening to the client's overview of negative experiences, actively probing recent positive events or helpful changes, correcting the bias of only focusing on the negative, obtaining more comprehensive recent information.
675.when_to_use: In the 'obtaining the latest information' process in the opening segment, after the client has reported a negative experience, to balance the information and complete the understanding of the recent situation.
675.trigger: When the client only describes negative events, with a low tone, not yet spontaneously mentioning any positive experiences or improvement signs.

676.skill_name: Facilitate summarized reporting to avoid getting lost in details
676.skill_description: Prompt explicitly that only 'the general gist or the title of the matter' is needed, guide the client to summarize in a short title or bullet points, avoiding detailed accounts of the process and the minutiae, saving time in the opening part and leaving room for processing in the middle part.
676.when_to_use: When obtaining the latest information, the client begins to detail the process along the timeline or expand a large amount of background, resulting in too much information, beyond the summary needed for the opening step.
676.trigger: Clues that the client lays out event details one by one, repeatedly supplements process information, or deviates from a summary review.

677.skill_name: Add items needing deeper discussion to the agenda
677.skill_description: For life events the client thinks need in-depth discussion, temporarily not expanding on them, recording and adding them to today's agenda list, arranging discussion in the middle phase, maintaining session structure and efficiency.
677.when_to_use: When collecting recent situations at the start phase, identifying that an event is complex and related to this session's goals, needing technical handling in the middle phase.
677.trigger: The client indicates that something needs to be discussed or hopes to focus on solving it, or the matter exceeds the outline level and involves refinement of problem handling.

678.skill_description: At the start phase, following the process to jointly verify with the client whether the last assigned Homework was completed, to what extent, and how. Routine checking can play a supervisory role, avoiding weakened motivation for completing homework due to not checking, and providing a basis for subsequent discussion.
678.when_to_use: At the start of subsequent Consultative sessions, after completing mood assessment and Obtaining the latest information, entering the third task of Reviewing homework, for routine checking and Reinforcing execution motivation.
678.trigger: The client mentions the homework assigned last time or briefly reports its implementation, or waits at the opening component to be asked about the homework.

679.skill_description: Based on the content and execution experience of the client's completed homework, extract information reflecting symptom and functioning changes, to judge counseling progress and intervention effects, clarify whether current change is improvement or stagnation, and guide the focus of subsequent sessions.
679.when_to_use: In the process of reviewing the homework, it is necessary to understand the changes during the period from the last session to this session, to serve as the basis for measuring counseling progress.
679.trigger: When the client, while reporting on homework, describes the experience, results, or changes after carrying it out, such as changed feelings, adjusted behavior, or maintaining the status quo.

680.skill_name: Incorporating key homework points into the agenda
680.skill_description: When reviewing homework, identifying content needing further discussion or handling, briefly recording its key points and adding them to this session's agenda list, arranging targeted discussion and handling in the middle phase.
680.when_to_use: When setting and confirming the agenda at the opening stage, homework-related content that needs in-depth discussion is discovered while reviewing the homework.
680.trigger: The client mentions content needing further discussion in the homework report (such as homework-related matters needing clarification, extension, or handling).

690.skill_description: At the ending stage, jointly clarify with the client the homework items to be completed after this session, list concrete items through two-way confirmation, preparing for subsequent assessment of willingness and possible problems, avoiding vague or omitted homework.
690.when_to_use: At the ending phase of the first or subsequent Consultative sessions, when preparing to wrap up, needing to ensure clear post-session action directions and forming a concrete homework list.
690.trigger: When the client has not yet actively mentioned homework arrangements, or describes what to do after going back vaguely and hesitantly, not yet forming clear homework items.

691.skill_name: Ask about homework feasibility and problems
691.skill_description: In Session feedback, using standardized Questioning, directly asking 'Regarding Homework, how likely are you to complete it? What problems might arise?', to understand the client's willingness to complete and possible obstacles and thoughts.
691.when_to_use: The session feedback stage of the closing component, after the homework content has been preliminarily determined, when implementation feasibility and potential obstacles need to be assessed.
691.trigger: When the client shows uncertainty or worry about homework execution, or gives a subjective assessment of completion possibility when answering feedback questions and raises difficulty points.

692.skill_name: Adjusting homework strategies by willingness level
692.skill_description: Make decisions based on the client's self-assessment of the possibility of completion: if the willingness is below 50%, drop the assignment; if the willingness is between 50%-80%, list the assignment as an optional task, and confirm the final list accordingly.
692.when_to_use: After completing the assessment of the likelihood of homework completion, when preparing to finally confirm or adjust the homework list and form.
692.trigger: When the client rates completion possibility as below 50% or between 50%–80%, or clearly expresses unwillingness, low confidence, and other low-willingness signals.

624.skill_name: Establishing an emotion scale and obtaining ratings
624.skill_description: Showing the client the 0–100% emotion scale, explaining 0 as none and 100% as extremely strong, drawing the scale on paper when necessary, clarifying that the rating target is the identified target emotion, and asking them to give the current intensity value, as a pre-Intervention baseline.
624.when_to_use: Within a single agenda, when the target emotion and related Automatic thoughts have been identified, before preparing to start Intervention, needing to establish a quantitative baseline for subsequent comparison.
624.trigger: When the client reports specific emotions (such as tension, fear, embarrassment) but not yet quantified, or the counselor is preparing to enter the phase of 'next, assessing the degree of thoughts and emotions'.

625.skill_name: Using the anchoring comparison method to determine emotion ratings
625.skill_description: When it is difficult to determine the score, guiding the client to recall or imagine the 100% extreme situation of that emotion, focusing on physiological feelings like heartbeat and breathing, then comparing current feelings with it; imagining different-score scenarios when necessary, helping determine a clear number.
625.when_to_use: During emotion rating, when the client is unsure about the score, wavering among multiple numbers, needing calibration and decision.
625.trigger: When the client says 'unable to determine' or hesitates among 50%, 60%, 70%, with a hesitant tone or embarrassed expression, finding it difficult to give a definite number.

626.skill_name: Establishes a belief scale and obtains baseline ratings of automatic thoughts
626.skill_description: Drawing and explaining the 0–100% belief scale, explaining the meaning of complete belief and complete disbelief, emphasizing that most are partial beliefs; asking the client to give the current degree of belief in the identified Automatic thoughts, forming a pre-Intervention baseline rating.
626.when_to_use: Within a single agenda, when the Automatic thoughts content needing assessment is clear, before formally launching cognitive or behavioral Intervention, needing to quantify the degree of belief.
626.trigger: When the client has clearly expressed an Automatic thought (such as 'I will not pass') but has not yet rated the degree of belief, or the counselor is preparing to assess their confidence.

627.skill_name: Explaining the rating purpose to improve cooperation
627.skill_description: Briefly explain that ratings are used to quantify progress and session effectiveness, helping both parties judge change; inform them that ratings will be carried out repeatedly and that with practice they will become more proficient and quicker, in order to improve cooperation and consistency in assessment.
627.when_to_use: When first introducing the emotion/belief rating tool, or the client doubts the meaning of rating and cooperates insufficiently.
627.trigger: When the client says 'do not understand why we are doing this' or shows confusion and resistance toward repeated rating, needing to enhance motivation and understanding.

628.skill_name: Re-evaluating after Intervention to test effects
628.skill_description: After completing the cognitive or behavioral intervention, invite the client to use the same scale to re-assess the intensity of the target emotion and the degree of belief in the automatic thought, and compare them with the pre-intervention values to objectively examine the session effect and the immediate change.
628.when_to_use: After completing one round of Intervention within an agenda, when needing to assess immediate effectiveness and judge whether to continue deepening or move to summary.
628.trigger: When the Intervention steps end or the client subjectively reports changes like 'worries reduced somewhat', needing to verify and quantify progress digitally.

629.skill_name: Record ratings in counseling notes to track progress
629.skill_description: Guide the client to record thought content, emotion names, assessment times and counts, and corresponding scores in counseling notes, forming a traceable quantitative record, facilitating subsequent horizontal comparison and showing progress, and consolidating assessment and self-monitoring habits.
629.when_to_use: Used after obtaining baseline or re-evaluation data, when objective records need to be kept for cross-session comparison and progress tracking.
629.trigger: Emotion and belief ratings are completed in the session, and the counselor is preparing to 'write down these two ratings', or the client has a notebook at hand ready for use.

649.skill_name: Guiding completion of the first four columns of basic information
649.skill_description: Guiding the client to first complete the four columns of date and time, situation, automatic thoughts and their degree of belief, and emotions and their intensity, laying the material and scoring baseline for subsequent evaluation.
649.when_to_use: At the initial assessment stage of starting to use the Thought record sheet, preparing to move from identification to evaluation, establishing a complete record for a single event.
649.trigger: The client reports just having experienced obvious emotion, can already describe the situation and state the automatic thought at the time, or has completed monitoring table entries and is preparing to expand.

650.skill_name: Asking about supporting and contradicting evidence
650.skill_description: In 'appropriate responses', guide the client to list evidence supporting the automatic thought and evidence supporting the opposite idea, evaluating effectiveness by factual comparison.
650.when_to_use: Entering the evaluation segment of the thought record form, when the evidence method needs to be used to test the truth and bias of automatic thoughts.
650.trigger: The client gives a high degree of belief to the automatic thought (such as 90-100%) and insists on the original thought with 'this is just a fact'.

651.skill_description: Guiding the client to propose multiple possible interpretations for the same situation, recording different interpretations to reduce single, speculative attribution.
651.when_to_use: After evidence comparison, the client still clings to a single-path inference, and cognitive possibilities need to be broadened.
651.trigger: The client simplifies events into single causes or presents only one explanation, finding it hard to see other possibilities.

652.skill_name: Assess worst, best, and most realistic outcomes
652.skill_description: Requiring the client to state the worst, best outcomes, as well as the most realistic and likely outcome, helping calibrate catastrophizing Anticipation.
652.when_to_use: When extreme, catastrophizing tendencies appear in situation Anticipation, correcting through three-stage outcome comparison.
652.trigger: When the client uses catastrophizing language like 'it is over' or 'will definitely fail', or is unsure about outcome probabilities.

653.skill_name: Comparing the impact of belief and change
653.skill_description: Having the client separately write down the impact of sticking with the original Automatic thoughts and the impact of changing thoughts, examining their contribution to goals by usefulness standards.
653.when_to_use: When Automatic thoughts may be valid but useless, needing to shift to functional assessment to promote goal achievement.
653.trigger: The client emphasizes 'it is true' while ignoring whether it helps the goal, or progress toward the goal is hindered by cognition.

654.skill_description: Guide the client to produce gentler, more reasonable self-persuasion statements by way of 'what would I say if someone else met the same situation'.
654.when_to_use: When self-talk is harsh and self-soothing is difficult, using others' perspectives to increase the acceptability of alternative thoughts.
654.trigger: The client is excessively self-critical, or when their answers stall or are hard to produce, perspective-taking is needed to generate suggestions.

655.skill_description: Under the question 'what should I do?', clarifying the next executable behavior and recording it as an action plan for later application and consolidation.
655.when_to_use: After the cognitive discussion is complete, alternative thoughts need to be turned into concrete behaviors so the change can be implemented.
655.trigger: When the client says 'do not know what to do' or has formed new ideas but lacks executable steps.

656.skill_name: Rating alternative responses item by item
656.skill_description: Ask the client to mark the degree of belief for each new thought in the 'adaptive responses', forming a contrast to screen for more believable alternative thoughts.
656.when_to_use: After multiple alternative thoughts are generated, when quantitative comparison is needed to determine the priority cognitive response to adopt.
656.trigger: The client writes out several alternative thoughts but has difficulty choosing among them, or the counselor wants to cultivate a habit of quantitative assessment.

657.skill_name: Filling in the conclusion column to summarize
657.skill_description: In the conclusion, record the degree of belief in the automatic thought after this evaluation, changes in emotional intensity, and the behavior the client is prepared to take, forming a closed loop.
657.when_to_use: After completing the 'suitable response', the amount of change in this round's cognition and emotion and the action intentions need to be summarized.
657.trigger: The client has finished answering the evaluation questions and enters the wrap-up stage, needing to quantify change and clarify behaviors.

658.skill_name: Prompting that inapplicable questions can be skipped
658.skill_description: Informing the client that not every question applies; those unable to answer can be skipped, to maintain process fluidity and fit.
658.when_to_use: When items that do not fit or are difficult to answer appear during Thought record sheet filling, reducing burden.
658.trigger: When the client is unable to answer a standard question, finds it not fitting, showing hesitation or intensified Anxiety.

659.skill_name: Correcting usage deviations during the session
659.skill_description: When recording is ineffective, discussing item by item in the session and demonstrating correct answering methods, ensuring evaluation questions are correctly used.
659.when_to_use: When reviewing the client's Thought record sheet homework, discovering cognition and emotions have not yet improved or answering biases.
659.trigger: When the client reports 'answering did not work either', old belief scores not yet decreased, or emotional intensity unchanged.

642.skill_name: Explain the monitoring form and assign homework
642.skill_description: Explaining to the client the purpose and three-column structure (situations, Automatic thoughts, emotions) and date-time fields of the Automatic thought monitoring form, and assigning it after the first Consultative session as foundational Homework for identification practice.
642.when_to_use: When the first Consultative session ends, entering the Automatic thoughts Learning stage, needing to extend identification practice into daily life.
642.trigger: When the client asks how to practice identifying thoughts in life, or feels lost about 'how to start recording'.

643.skill_name: Starting to fill in when emotions arise
643.skill_description: Instructing the client to use emotions as clues: whenever they notice a certain emotion appearing, they begin filling in the monitoring form, as the entry point for capturing automatic thoughts and the starting point of recording.
643.when_to_use: In daily life or counseling sessions, when the client shows obvious emotional experiences, needing timely recording to identify thinking.
643.trigger: When the client reports or shows emotions like tension, embarrassment, Anxiety, accompanied by rapid heartbeat, breathing changes, or expression fluctuations.

644.skill_description: Teaching the standard filling order: 1 record emotion words; 2 fill in date-time and situation (real trigger); 3 notice and write Automatic thoughts/imagery; 4 assess the degree of belief in thoughts and emotional intensity.
644.when_to_use: When assigning homework or before the client starts filling it in for the first time, clear operating procedures need to be provided to reduce confusion.
644.trigger: When the client shows mixed-up entries, omissions, or says 'do not know what to write first, how to fill'.

645.skill_name: Instruct in percentage ratings of beliefs and emotions
645.skill_description: Requiring the client to give percentage ratings in the monitoring form for the degree of belief in automatic thoughts and the intensity of emotions, tracking the change effects of sessions and practice quantitatively.
645.when_to_use: After monitoring table entries are completed, needing to quantify the current state for subsequent comparison of changes before and after Intervention.
645.trigger: When the client has written the situation, Automatic thoughts, and emotions, but lacks or hesitates on ratings, with uncertain scores.

646.skill_name: Setting practice Anticipation and frequency reminders
646.skill_description: Emphasizing to the client that identifying is a skill needing practice; catching three to five initially is enough, adjusting expectations for homework completion, reducing self-blame and encouraging continued practice.
646.when_to_use: When first assigning the monitoring table homework or during early review, needing to calibrate practice goals and difficulty Anticipation.
646.trigger: When the client worries 'cannot remember/cannot grasp thoughts', is anxious about the number of entries, or self-criticizes due to slow progress.

647.skill_name: Allowing blanks temporarily with an agreement to fill in later
647.skill_description: Clarifying that if emotions can be identified but Automatic thoughts cannot currently be noticed, the Automatic thoughts column can be temporarily left blank, filling other items as usual, and agreeing to supplement them in the session.
647.when_to_use: When the client encounters identification bottlenecks during recording, affecting entry completeness, needing to maintain recording continuity.
647.trigger: When the client says 'do not know what I was thinking at the time' or still cannot write Automatic thoughts after multiple attempts.

648.skill_name: Reviewing the monitoring table and assisting identification with Questioning
648.skill_description: Reviewing the client's monitoring table in the session, using targeted Questioning to guide recalling situations for blank or vague entries, clarifying and supplementing Automatic thoughts content and corresponding ratings.
648.when_to_use: When reviewing homework each session, discovering monitoring table entries are incomplete or identification needs deepening.
648.trigger: When the Automatic thoughts column in the monitoring table is left blank or described vaguely, the client is unclear about thoughts at the time, needing counselor assistance.

630.skill_name: Make a coping card: define the situation and write the front and back
630.skill_description: Writing repeatedly triggering situations or Automatic thoughts on the front of the coping card with the client, and coping thoughts and behavioral instructions on the back; the card follows the principle of portability, facilitating carrying and use.
630.when_to_use: The consolidation segment of the automatic thought stage, when effective strategies need to be externalized into portable cue tools after the session.
630.trigger: When the client reports repeatedly experiencing negative emotions like Anxiety, worry, or self-blame and Automatic thoughts in similar situations.

631.skill_name: Jointly developing appropriate ideas and behavioral strategies for coping cards
631.skill_description: Together with the client, based on facts and goals, jointly discuss the most suitable beliefs and concrete behavioral steps for the situation, and record the key statements and action instructions on the back of a card for easy implementation.
631.when_to_use: When drafting or updating the coping card content, the session conclusions need to be converted into concise, feasible self-instructions.
631.trigger: When the client is clear about distress in certain scenarios but lacks effective coping ideas, or reserve concepts and behaviors are not yet formed.

632.skill_name: Explaining the coping card's use and review process
632.skill_description: Clarifying daily morning and evening card review; when encountering trigger situations, taking out the card and repeatedly reading until emotions weaken, then implementing behaviors per the card's instructions, to form a stable self-help routine.
632.when_to_use: When assigning Homework and application, needing to concretize the coping card's use method into a daily process.
632.trigger: When the client is willing to try the coping card or asks how to specifically use it, when to review, how to handle emotions not yet relieved.

633.skill_name: Guiding the writing of counseling notes and organizing key points by item
633.skill_description: After the agenda ends, jointly reviewing the transferable cognitive and behavioral points, marking the date and recording them item by item, forming counseling notes convenient for later review and application.
633.when_to_use: At the end of each agenda item or session, used to consolidate new thoughts and behavioral plans, preparing to take them back to life scenarios for application.
633.trigger: When the client shows insight in the discussion or forms alternative thoughts and behavioral plans, these need to be solidified into reviewable materials.

634.skill_name: Ask the client to review counseling notes daily for consolidation
634.skill_description: Clarifying daily scheduled time to review counseling notes, Reinforcing memory and transfer application, improving counseling effectiveness and shortening the course.
634.when_to_use: At session summary and homework assignment, emphasizing daily practice for consolidation and self-help ability improvement.
634.trigger: The client worries about forgetting session key points, hopes to speed up improvement, or needs to establish a stable review habit.

635.skill_name: Assign the four-step automatic-thought monitoring form homework
635.skill_description: Teaches and requires filling in the monitoring form when emotions appear: naming the emotion, recording the date and situation, perceiving automatic thoughts, evaluating the degree of belief in the thoughts and the intensity of the emotion.
635.when_to_use: After the first Consultative session, entering the skill Learning stage, used to practice identifying thoughts and emotions in life.
635.trigger: When the client can already identify current emotions, expressing the wish to capture Automatic thoughts in daily life for practice.

636.skill_name: Setting monitoring homework Anticipation and tolerance handling
636.skill_description: Explaining that capturing few thoughts at the beginning is normal; allowing the automatic thoughts column to be left blank for now, promising to help fill it in and correct it next session, reducing homework pressure and maintaining practice.
636.when_to_use: When assigning the automatic thought monitoring form task, need to prevent frustration and maintain compliance.
636.trigger: When the client says 'cannot write out thoughts' or 'worrying about doing it poorly', or has too high expectations for practice effects and quantity.

637.skill_name: Assign thought records and teach the six-question method
637.skill_description: Guiding the use of the six standard 'suitable response' questions to systematically evaluate Automatic thoughts, and rating newly emerged responses item by item, cultivating assessment habits of effectiveness and usefulness.
637.when_to_use: When the client has preliminarily mastered identification, entering the evaluation skill's consolidation and application training.
637.trigger: The client is able to complete monitoring forms and proposes wanting to further learn to evaluate and change thinking.

638.skill_name: Guide conclusion-writing and form a behavioral plan
638.skill_description: In the conclusion column of the thought record form, updating the believability of the old thought and the emotional intensity, clarifying the concrete behavior steps to be taken, so the cognitive change is implemented into action.
638.when_to_use: When practicing or reviewing the thought record form, turning evaluation results into actionable plans.
638.trigger: When the client has completed the 'suitable response' but has not yet integrated an action plan or updated ratings.

639.skill_name: Correct thought-record misuse within the session
639.skill_description: Reviewing homework and for 'ineffective' feedback, demonstrating correct answers and applying the six-question method item by item, refilling together when necessary, ensuring the method is correct before continuing consolidation.
639.when_to_use: At the homework review and consolidation stage, discovering the record form is improperly used or ineffective.
639.trigger: When the client reports 'answered the six questions but did not improve/belief degree not yet decreased' or says they do not know how to use it.

640.skill_name: Provide record format options to balance privacy and portability
640.skill_description: Choose the form of recording coping cards and notes according to preference, such as pen and paper or phone recording, reducing privacy-exposure concerns and improving the convenience of carrying and review.
640.when_to_use: When planning recording and review methods, needing to improve compliance and sustainability.
640.trigger: When the client is uncomfortable with the writing notebook, worries about privacy or finds carrying inconvenient, proposing to switch to other forms.

641.skill_name: Implement alternative thoughts and alternative behaviors in daily life practice
641.skill_description: Converting the new thoughts and new behaviors obtained in the session into concrete life requirements, clarifying to think with the new thoughts and act with the new behaviors in corresponding situations, ensuring application is put into practice.
641.when_to_use: The consolidation and application stage, setting concrete practice requirements and scenes before leaving the consulting room.
641.trigger: The client has formed alternative thoughts or alternative behaviors and is ready to return to daily life to face the same situations.

611.skill_name: First identifying emotions then probing Automatic thoughts
611.skill_description: First assisting the client to notice and accurately name the currently prominent emotion, then probing the Automatic thoughts at the time in that specific situation, clarifying model elements, paving the way for subsequent assessment and Intervention.
611.when_to_use: At the concretization of the automatic-thought stage agenda or the start of a topic, the situation, emotion, and thought need to be locked in; the client cooperates and emotional reactions are obvious.
611.trigger: The client shows marked emotions such as tension, sadness or anger, or physiological / verbal changes, such as a faster heartbeat, trembling hands, sighing, or a change in speech rate.

612.skill_name: Providing an emotion vocabulary list to assist naming
612.skill_description: When the client finds it hard to describe emotions with words, handing them the negative emotion vocabulary list, inviting them to select fitting words and confirm, completing accurate naming for subsequent thought identification.
612.when_to_use: At the emotion identification stage; at the first session or when the client's emotion vocabulary is poor and naming is difficult, the goal is completing precise labeling.
612.trigger: When the client says 'cannot say it well', 'do not know which word to use', 'unable to describe the mood', showing confusion or Silence.

613.skill_name: Clarifying the meanings of similar emotion words
613.skill_description: Explain the differences between similar emotions (such as tension and fear) in terms of situation and sense of threat, and in light of the person's circumstances help them choose a more fitting label, reducing confusion.
613.when_to_use: When the client hesitates between two emotion words or names inaccurately; needing to improve emotion identification precision for subsequent thought probing.
613.trigger: When the client mentions two similar emotions simultaneously and is uncertain, such as 'tension also feels like fear', showing an uncertain tone.

614.skill_name: Observing expressions and nonverbal cues to identify emotions
614.skill_description: Inferring current emotions through changes in facial, postural, and speech expressions (such as hand trembling, restlessness, trembling voice), and asking accordingly to confirm and name.
614.when_to_use: When needing to quickly grasp emotions in the session or discovering the narrative does not match expression, used to initiate emotion identification and subsequent probing.
614.trigger: Contradictory manifestations or obvious signs of tension such as clenching teeth, sweating, avoiding eye contact, speech rate fluctuating between fast and slow, and forcing a relaxed demeanor.

615.skill_name: Pointing out and distinguishing emotions from thoughts
615.skill_description: When the client confuses emotions with thoughts, clearly explaining that emotions are subjective feelings and thoughts are cognitive content, requiring separate word reporting, establishing correct distinction.
615.when_to_use: When confusion appears at the identification stage, needing to improve reporting accuracy, providing clear input for subsequent assessment.
615.trigger: The client expresses emotions as 'I think...' or treats thoughts as emotions, such as 'I am too nervous, that is just thinking', with confused semantics.

616.skill_name: Directly asking open-ended questions about automatic thoughts
616.skill_description: After clarifying the situation, using open-ended Questioning like 'What are you thinking/What did you say to yourself/What thought surfaced?' to prompt the client to report immediate Automatic thoughts.
616.when_to_use: After emotions are identified or the situation is concretized, entering the thought identification stage to obtain original thoughts.
616.trigger: When the client just described the problem and shows emotions like Anxiety and embarrassment, appearing willing to communicate and mentally present.

617.skill_description: Based on the named emotion, asking 'when you feel X, what are you thinking?' to capture automatic thoughts at the emotion-thought connection point, improving the retrieval hit rate.
617.when_to_use: After obtaining a clear emotion label, the corresponding automatic thought needs to be located to advance the conceptualization.
617.trigger: When the client says specific emotion words like 'losing face', 'very anxious', 'embarrassed', and recalls the situation at the time.

618.skill_name: Inviting the client to infer thoughts at the time
618.skill_description: For clients unable to report directly, inviting them to try inferring possible thoughts based on the situation at the time, reducing retrieval difficulty and providing clues for subsequent confirmation.
618.when_to_use: When direct Questioning yields no results and the client's self-awareness is weak, used to indirectly obtain thought clues.
618.trigger: When the client answers 'I was not thinking anything', 'cannot explain clearly', 'cannot remember', accompanied by hesitation or Silence.

619.skill_name: Offer options or opposite cues to elicit thinking
619.skill_description: Proposing one or two possible or opposite thoughts as option prompts, asking 'Are you thinking... or...?' to induce the client to identify and confirm their Automatic thoughts.
619.when_to_use: When the client is silent or hesitant and has difficulty locating specific thoughts, external prompts are needed to activate statements.
619.trigger: When there is prolonged Silence, head shaking, indecision, only vague answers to questions, or no answer.

620.skill_name: Rationally analyzing 'what it means' to elicit thoughts
620.skill_description: Guiding discussion of 'what does this situation mean to you', reasoning to restore more core Automatic thoughts through rational analysis of situational meaning for identification.
620.when_to_use: When other Questioning methods work poorly, needing abstract-concrete conversion to reach thoughts.
620.trigger: When the client can think but finds it hard to directly verbalize thoughts, responding 'also cannot explain clearly' or 'probably not'.

621.skill_name: Guiding situational reenactment and slowing the process
621.skill_description: Invite the client to reproduce in their mind the time, place, and process of that moment, slowing the reproduction speed when necessary, until the automatic thought of that time emerges and is captured.
621.when_to_use: When memory is vague or thoughts are hard to grasp, handling identification and retrospection of specific situations.
621.trigger: When the client says 'cannot remember at the time' or 'only remember being very nervous', finding it difficult to recall details or with jumping thoughts.

622.skill_name: Using Empathy to propose alternative thoughts for verification
622.skill_description: The counselor empathically puts themselves in the client's situation, proposing possible thoughts for verification and selection, as an auxiliary path for identifying Automatic thoughts, triggering self-awareness.
622.when_to_use: When multiple identification methods still have not worked, needing an external model to help the client locate thoughts.
622.trigger: When the client acknowledges the counselor's understanding but still cannot produce specific thoughts, showing repeated denial or confusion.

623.skill_name: Temporarily suspending identification and arranging re-awareness in situations
623.skill_description: When multiple methods are still ineffective, temporarily abandoning current identification, instructing to actively notice and record Automatic thoughts when similar situations reappear, leaving them for subsequent sessions.
623.when_to_use: At the end of the identification process, when session time is limited or identification has no progress, as a subsequent arrangement.
623.trigger: After multiple attempts, still no thought reports at all, the client appears frustrated or tired, saying 'talk about it later'.

552.skill_name: Clarifying and writing down automatic thoughts
552.skill_description: According to the prosecution-defense process, first clarifying and recording the client's core automatic thought, as the base of the prosecution's claim, ensuring the discussion object is focused and operable.
552.when_to_use: At the initial assessment stage, when starting to apply the prosecution-defense technique, needing to focus on this Intervention's thought goals and entering the evidence-presenting process.
552.trigger: When the client summarizes their worry or judgment in one sentence, such as 'cannot fail again' or 'will retaliate against me', and develops emotions around it.

553.skill_name: Correct evidence standards to distinguish inference from fact
553.skill_description: Point out that inference or assumption is not evidence, emphasizing that evidence is the concrete events that have occurred; guide a return to past experience to support or refute the idea.
553.when_to_use: At the early stage of prosecution-defense evidence presentation, when the client's initially given 'evidence' is mostly inferences, analyses, or future assumptions.
553.trigger: When the client uses reasoning like 'too little time to possibly turn things around' or 'must win it back this time' as evidence, lacking facts that have already happened.

554.skill_description: Under the prosecution's stance, probe into past facts supporting the automatic thought, record specific events one by one, limited to situations that objectively occurred.
554.when_to_use: The automatic thought is already clear, and it is time to enter the prosecution side (supporting the automatic thought) to present evidence and collect relevant facts.
554.trigger: The client has already offered one or a few supporting examples, and more prosecution-side evidence needs to be systematically developed and supplemented.

555.skill_name: Guiding the defense's claims and evidence
555.skill_description: Put forward a claim opposite to the automatic thought, asking the client to collect past facts supporting the defense side, completing the reverse evidence to balance the cognition.
555.when_to_use: When prosecution evidence has been collected or one side dominates, the defense's arguments and evidence need to be developed to avoid one-sided generalization.
555.trigger: When the client says 'seems like there is nothing more' or only provides one-sided evidence, with obviously imbalanced positive and negative information.

556.skill_description: During the prosecution-defense evidence presentation, using continuous questioning, prompting the client to supplement more evidence from different times and areas, improving sample adequacy.
556.when_to_use: When the evidence-collection process stalls or the amount is small, and the evidence scope and depth need to be expanded.
556.trigger: When the client pauses after providing one or two items, saying 'seems like there is nothing more', or only focusing on a different situation.

557.skill_name: Structured recording on the prosecution-defense form
557.skill_description: Using the prosecution-defense technique table to present Automatic thoughts, both sides' claims and evidence, and reasonable conclusions, organizing information for comprehensive weighing and review.
557.when_to_use: When there is much evidence and verbal accounts are easily confused, the pros and cons information needs to be clearly presented and summarized to form a conclusion.
557.trigger: When the client involves multiple lines of supporting and opposing evidence and claims, hard to organize in verbal discussion.

558.skill_name: Integrate pros and cons evidence to form a reasonable conclusion
558.skill_description: After both sides have finished presenting evidence, guide the client to weigh the evidence and arrive at an alternative thought, and write it into the 'reasonable conclusion' to correct the original cognition.
558.when_to_use: Pros and cons evidence has been gathered, and the discussion needs to be wrapped up to produce a new, more reasonable alternative thought.
558.trigger: The client has listed multiple pieces of evidence for both prosecution and defense, and expresses willingness to re-evaluate and form a conclusion.

559.skill_description: Identifying the associated belief hierarchy, prioritizing Intervention on the foundational beliefs in the derivation chain, to improve the prosecution-defense technique's targeting and effectiveness.
559.when_to_use: Two or more interrelated automatic thoughts exist, and the primary and secondary ones need to be distinguished with a focus on the key link.
559.trigger: The second belief is clearly built on the first belief, e.g. 'will retaliate' giving rise to 'will fire me'.

560.skill_name: Assisting in expanding the defense's evidence
560.skill_description: The counselor proactively inspires the client to seek defense evidence from more situations and time periods, increasing the counter-samples, promoting cognition from biased toward balanced.
560.when_to_use: When the defense's evidence is insufficient, thin, or overly concentrated, needing to expand the evidence base.
560.trigger: The client's defense examples are few, mostly single cases, hard to support the opposite claim.

561.skill_name: Apply the conclusion to verify in the current situation
561.skill_description: Facilitate the client to apply the reasonable conclusion to his own recent interactions, compare the signs before and after giving the opinion, examine the degree of fit, and observe the emotional changes.
561.when_to_use: A reasonable conclusion has been formed, when it needs to be verified in real situations and the cognitive-correction effect consolidated.
561.trigger: When the client still feels worried or uncomfortable, doubting whether post-event interactions will change, needing on-site verification and comparison.

562.skill_name: Clarifying current objective facts or phenomena
562.skill_description: Guiding the client to define the objective facts triggering emotions in concise sentences (such as not yet answering the phone, the child not yet returning), shifting attention from speculation to observable situations, laying the foundation for subsequent generation of multiple interpretations and verification actions.
562.when_to_use: At the starting stage of the Divergent thinking technique, used to clarify the Anxiety source and situation, with the goal of grounding vague worries in concrete facts, facilitating subsequent possibility analysis.
562.trigger: When the client repeatedly speculates in Unknown situations, with language like 'will it or not...' or 'unease'; accompanied by pacing back and forth, finding it hard to get things done, such as parents showing obvious Anxiety because the child has not yet returned.

563.skill_name: Clarifying and fixing the initial single explanation
563.skill_description: After facts are clear, asking the client to clearly state their current single interpretation or Automatic thoughts (such as 'he is unwilling to answer' or 'got into a car accident'), fixing it orally or in writing as a reference baseline, facilitating subsequent divergence to generate other possibilities.
563.when_to_use: After clarifying objective facts, before entering interpretation generation; the goal is identifying and externalizing the client's current dominant interpretation, providing a starting point for comparison and expansion.
563.trigger: The client directly gives a negative, single explanation, such as 'he finds me troublesome' or 'the child has been abducted', and emotions run high accordingly.

564.skill_name: Consecutive questioning to elicit diverse explanations
564.skill_description: Using open-ended Questioning and continuous follow-ups like 'what else?' or 'any other interpretations?', prompting the client to propose more possible interpretations from different angles, avoiding staying with the worst interpretation, systematically expanding the interpretation list.
564.when_to_use: At the divergent stage, the goal is to broaden the cognitive perspective and increase the number of candidate explanations, providing material for later evidence and probability evaluation.
564.trigger: When the client stays only with one or two negative possibilities, using absolutist words like 'definitely' or 'inevitably', or saying 'do not know anymore'.

565.skill_description: When the client is exhausted, guiding them to think 'if this happened to someone else, how would they interpret it?' Using others' frameworks to inspire new ideas, emphasizing that the client proposes them, not thinking for them.
565.when_to_use: When explanation generation is blocked, used to relieve thought stuckness and continue expanding explanations; the goal is to restore the client's active thinking.
565.trigger: When the client says 'cannot think of any more', stays Silent or shrugs, expecting the counselor to directly give answers.

566.skill_name: Collecting supporting evidence for each explanation
566.skill_description: For each explanation, guide the client to search for supporting evidence, which can come from direct experience, analogies of surrounding situations, or environmental information; allow some explanations to temporarily lack evidence and record them to be supplemented, avoiding relying only on guessing.
566.when_to_use: After the explanation list is formed, entering the evidence stage; the goal is to use facts to screen the plausibility of explanations and reduce speculation.
566.trigger: When the client admits insufficient understanding, cannot provide direct evidence, or only uses subjective speculation to support an interpretation; needing supplementary evidence from surrounding experience and information.

567.skill_name: Quantifying each explanation's probability with percentages
567.skill_description: Assisting the client to give percentage estimates for each interpretation, comparing relative probabilities; reducing vague Anxiety through quantification, and setting priorities for subsequent verification actions.
567.when_to_use: Used after evidence organization, upon entering the assessment stage; the goal is to structure subjective judgments and form a comparable probability distribution.
567.trigger: The client is overly certain of a single explanation or finds it hard to weigh multiple possibilities, and emotional judgment affects decision-making.

568.skill_name: Designing and implementing a verification action plan
568.skill_description: Together with the explanations and probabilities, jointly formulate low-risk, feasible verification measures, such as making contact again at a different time, calling from another number, contacting the homeroom teacher or a peer's parent, or searching along the way, obtaining real evidence through behavior.
568.when_to_use: After probability assessment is complete, entering the action verification stage; the goal is testing each interpretation with actual behavior, alleviating uncertainty and Anxiety.
568.trigger: When interpretations and probabilities are formed but the client is still distressed, wanting to 'figure out the truth', or expressing continued Anxiety and suspicion.

569.skill_name: Keeping the client actively engaged with heuristic Questioning
569.skill_description: Throughout the technique application, using heuristic Questioning to have the client personally generate interpretations and evidence, avoiding the counselor substituting thinking; emphasizing client engagement to improve session effectiveness and self-help ability.
569.when_to_use: Continuously using throughout the divergent thinking process; the goal is ensuring the client as the main agent, enhancing intrinsic motivation for thinking and verification.
569.trigger: When the client only listens, not responding to Questioning, or Demands the counselor directly give conclusions and plans, with declining engagement.

570.skill_description: Around events not yet occurred, guiding the client to clarify the worst, most ideal, and most likely three outcomes, forming a possibility region from worst to best, laying the framework for subsequent evidence assessment and plan formulation.
570.when_to_use: At the initial assessment stage, when handling Anxiety or depression related to future events, initiating the Possibility-region technique to define the outcome range.
570.trigger: When the client makes negative or pessimistic predictions about events not yet occurred, such as 'exam ranking will drop beyond 20th' or 'when old will have no one to rely on', accompanied by obvious Anxiety/depression.

571.skill_name: Collecting and verifying evidence for worst and ideal outcomes
571.skill_description: Separately requiring the client to list specific evidence or signs (performance, experiences, facts) supporting the worst and most ideal outcomes, distinguishing speculation from evidence, providing a basis for subsequent judgment.
571.when_to_use: After clarifying the range of possibilities, facts are needed to support the extreme outcomes at both ends, avoiding reliance on subjective speculation alone.
571.trigger: The client proposes extreme possibilities but mainly based on reasoning or worry, lacking objective 'signs/manifestations' support; the evidence is one-sided.

572.skill_name: Synthesizing evidence to determine the most likely outcome
572.skill_description: After collecting unfavorable and favorable evidence, guiding the client to comprehensively weigh, clarifying the current most likely specific outcome (such as a ranking range), to correct overly negative Anticipation.
572.when_to_use: After sorting out pros and cons evidence, the information needs to be integrated into a more reasonable 'most likely outcome'.
572.trigger: When bidirectional evidence already exists (such as English progress coexisting with weak math), but the client still stays with extreme Anticipation or wavers.

573.skill_name: Planning coping strategies for the worst-case scenario
573.skill_description: Directly inviting the client to think 'what to do once the worst happens', formulating an executable coping plan, helping them calmly face the worst possibility, reducing Fear and helplessness.
573.when_to_use: When the client keeps worrying about the worst outcome, needing to improve the sense of control through concrete plans, alleviating Anxiety.
573.trigger: The client repeatedly asks or associates to 'what if the worst happens', showing signs of tension and intensifying worry.

574.skill_name: Planning actions to strive for better outcomes
574.skill_description: When the event has not yet occurred, discussing concrete measures with the client to improve outcomes (such as increasing review, consulting others), shifting focus to actionable improvement behaviors.
574.when_to_use: After assessing the possibility range, the cognitive adjustment needs to be converted into an action plan oriented toward the ideal outcome.
574.trigger: The client expresses 'can I do something about it' or is willing to try to improve, and there are factors in the situation that can be actively influenced.

575.skill_name: Inspire expansion of ideal possible resource options
575.skill_description: When the client has difficulty imagining ideal outcomes, inspiring them to expand their ideas from the perspective of resources such as government, community, and relatives' and friends' support, enriching the best possible paths and pictures.
575.when_to_use: When discussing 'the most ideal situation' and thinking is restricted, an external-resource perspective is needed to expand possibilities.
575.trigger: When the client says 'cannot imagine' the 'ideal outcome', stays Silent, or only stays with pessimistic assumptions.

576.skill_name: Assign information-gathering homework to refine the assessment
576.skill_description: When unable to determine the 'most likely situation', assigning homework for the client to go back and collect real information (policies, others' cases, life data), bringing it back next time to complete the assessment.
576.when_to_use: When materials in the session are insufficient and the client finds it difficult to give the most likely outcome, needing information supplementation outside the session.
576.trigger: When the client repeatedly says 'cannot think of it' regarding the 'most likely situation', with current evidence and understanding clearly insufficient.

577.skill_name: Shifting to behavioral experiments to gather evidence
577.skill_description: When facts supporting or refuting the automatic thought are both lacking, invites the client to design and carry out a behavioral experiment to generate observable results as evidence, testing and correcting the belief.
577.when_to_use: When evidence is insufficient after initial assessment or cognitive technique application, at the stage of evaluating Automatic thoughts, needing to generate evidence through behavior to advance cognitive change.
577.trigger: When the client cannot provide past actually-occurred supporting or refuting cases, repeatedly saying 'no evidence' or 'cannot think of any'.

578.skill_description: For the first experiment, prioritizing less threatening times or scenarios (such as the lunch break rather than workday early morning), reducing the risk of adverse consequences, improving participation and execution willingness.
578.when_to_use: At the early stage of designing a behavioral experiment plan, when risk and feasibility need to be balanced to prompt action.
578.trigger: When the client emphasizes 'the consequences are very serious', showing obvious Anxiety or avoidance toward directly experimenting in the core situation.

579.skill_description: Agree with the client on the trial duration, frequency, and operational details (such as 40 minutes, lasting one week, waking before the alarm then continuing to sleep), ensuring consistent execution, facilitating result evaluation.
579.when_to_use: After determining the experiment situation and entering the implementation plan formulation stage, when it is necessary to refine execution standards.
579.trigger: When the client is unclear about specific operations or asks 'how to do it' 'how many times', or casual execution leads to unusable data.

580.skill_name: Using the Behavioral experiments record form
580.skill_description: Guide filling in the record form with the experiment time, situation, actual outcome, and the degree of belief in the old and new beliefs, forming trackable data for later assessment and decision-making.
580.when_to_use: During trial implementation and at each review, when belief changes need to be systematically recorded and quantified.
580.trigger: When the client finds it hard to recall experiment details, cannot quantify the degree of belief, with scattered information during review.

581.skill_description: Gradually approaching the core situation based on preliminary evidence (such as nap — rest day — workday, simulated flight — short trip — routine), Reinforcing new beliefs under controllable risk.
581.when_to_use: When initial experiments succeed and beliefs improve but the target threshold is not yet reached, needing to increase challenges to consolidate change.
581.trigger: When the client succeeds stably in low-risk experiments, still worrying about the core situation or old beliefs not yet significantly decreased.

582.skill_name: Evaluating and updating beliefs after the experiment
582.skill_description: After each experiment, quantify the degree of belief in the old belief and the alternative thought, and decide based on evidence to continue, adjust, or escalate the experiment, promoting continuous cognitive change.
582.when_to_use: At the end of the trial and stage reviews, used to revise plans and goals based on results.
582.trigger: When the client reports results after completing experiments, with changes in belief degree or indecision about the next step.

583.skill_name: Jointly design concrete behaviors to test new beliefs
583.skill_description: Guides the client to propose operable actions consistent with the new belief (such as facing it together, seeking relatives' support, comforting and relaxing), clarifies the time and executes them to verify the new belief.
583.when_to_use: A new belief has been proposed but acceptance is moderate, needing action to verify and consolidate alternative thinking.
583.trigger: When the client says 'do not understand what to do' or only partially believes the new belief (such as 30%), with insufficient willingness to act.

584.skill_name: Lowering action pressure with an experimental framework
584.skill_description: Clearly define the plan as an 'experiment', emphasizing the testing purpose and revocability, relieving tension and hesitation, and enhancing the motivation and feasibility of trying new behaviors.
584.when_to_use: When the client hesitates about action and is under great pressure, the emotional burden needs to be lowered to prompt the first step.
584.trigger: When the client expresses 'somewhat worried' or 'dare not do it', or shows Tension, avoidant behaviors.

585.skill_name: Use indirect experiments to collect real-world data
585.skill_description: When direct behavior is not feasible or risk is high, designing alternative data verification tasks (randomly selecting the next day's flights, collecting flight results of people around) to accumulate evidence.
585.when_to_use: When needing to first build confidence and an evidence base, and direct experiments are temporarily unsuitable or unreachable.
585.trigger: When the client has strong Fear of direct action, obvious scenario limitations, or uncontrollable risk, still needing to advance verification.

586.skill_name: Rehearse key situations and develop coping plans
586.skill_description: Before entering the core experiment, conducting situational meditation and rehearsal, pretending to fully believe the alternative thought, and planning in advance the coping and crisis handling for when automatic thoughts appear.
586.when_to_use: Before entering a core situational experiment (such as a first flight), the sense of control and coping preparation need to be enhanced.
586.trigger: When the client still shows Anxiety, Anticipating Automatic thoughts will appear, requiring a concrete coping plan.

587.skill_name: Guide listing the costs and benefits of old beliefs
587.skill_description: Through Questioning 'what impact does believing old thoughts have on you', prompting the client to concretize the benefits and drawbacks of old beliefs (such as temporarily avoiding Anxiety vs interfering with review, taking time, etc.), providing clear material for subsequent weighing.
587.when_to_use: At the start of the cost-benefit analysis after the initial assessment, when the client still strongly believes the automatic thought and the emotions or functioning are affected.
587.trigger: When the client describes old thoughts bringing Anxiety and tension, review being interfered with, or emphasizes the benefits of maintaining old practices like 'no need for Anxiety, no need to face danger'.

588.skill_name: Guide listing the benefits and costs of new beliefs
588.skill_description: Ask 'what would be the effect of changing the thought?', helping the client clarify the benefits of adopting alternative thinking (hope, relaxation, improved efficiency) and the possible costs or risks, forming a complete comparison.
588.when_to_use: After the pros and cons of the old belief have been sorted out, beginning to explore the influence of alternative thinking, used to refine the two-sided list.
588.trigger: The client has limited identification with the new idea, or raises concerns such as 'what if it fails, there are risks', needing to concretize the pros and cons of the new belief.

589.skill_name: Compare the pros and cons of both views and facilitate a choice
589.skill_description: After the costs and benefits of old and new beliefs are clarified, directly Questioning 'which one is more advantageous', guiding the client to comprehensively weigh and clearly choose to adopt the more advantageous view.
589.when_to_use: After completing both sides' pros-and-cons lists, when the client still hesitates or has not yet made a cognitive choice.
589.trigger: When the client pauses, wavers, finds it hard to decide after stating both sides' pros and cons, or responds with 'still not sure'.

590.skill_name: Checking the pros and cons against evidence to correct trade-offs
590.skill_description: Combining Behavioral experiments or facts, examining whether the listed benefits and drawbacks actually occurred, pointing out that the new belief's drawbacks have not yet occurred while the old belief's drawbacks are real, to Reinforce choice motivation.
590.when_to_use: Used in the weighing or choosing stage, when the client overestimates risk with small-probability worries, or test results already exist that can be used for verification.
590.trigger: When usable evidence exists (such as multiple flights all being safe), but the client still insists on old worries with 'better safe than sorry'.

591.skill_name: Translate choices into specific action inquiries
591.skill_description: Once the client chooses to adopt the new idea, ask further 'what can you do to make it happen', prompting them to propose behavior plans consistent with the new belief and executable, to implement the change.
591.when_to_use: The client has chosen an alternative thought or tends to believe the new idea, and the cognitive choice needs to be put into behavior.
591.trigger: When the client says 'of course it is changing thoughts' or agrees with the new belief, but has not yet proposed concrete next steps.

592.skill_name: Prioritize and implement starting behaviors step by step
592.skill_description: When multiple actions are proposed, guides choosing the one easiest to operate and with the most willingness to do first, and after success expanding, to reduce pressure and resistance and raise the execution rate.
592.when_to_use: After action plans have been generated, when prioritization and gradual implementation are needed in order to raise feasibility and adherence.
592.trigger: When the client proposes multiple alternative behaviors (such as answering carefully, double-checking, ignoring hand trembling), or reveals 'under great pressure, do not know where to start'.

593.skill_name: Break actions down into checklists or steps
593.skill_description: Concretizing general strategies into an operable checklist of checkpoints and execution steps (such as listing error-prone points and checking them item by item), to improve behavioral implementation and monitorability.
593.when_to_use: When the specific behavior to implement is determined, but the expression is still vague, lacking operational details and Self-monitoring arrangements.
593.trigger: The client only says broad expressions like 'be more careful, double-check', needing guidance to formulate a checklist and execute by it.

594.skill_name: Weighing changing vs. not changing in resistance situations
594.skill_description: When resistance appears, guide comparing the benefits and costs of maintaining the old state and the benefits and risks of change, emphasizing the possibility of success and the feasibility of escaping suffering to raise motivation for change.
594.when_to_use: When promoting action or choosing a new belief, encountering resistance phenomena such as hesitation, procrastination, or defending the old state.
594.trigger: When the client emphasizes the benefits of maintaining the status quo (gaining attention, avoiding responsibility) or exaggerates change risks, worrying about failure and Self-denial.

595.skill_name: Reflecting and naming the client's emotions
595.skill_description: According to clues such as face and tone, introduce emotion awareness with gentle reflection, invite the client to make clear with words the current emotional state (such as 'frustrated', 'tense'), establishing a common language and focus for subsequent assessment and intervention.
595.when_to_use: At the initial assessment or when entering topics; when the client's emotions are prominent but not yet clearly named; needing to lay the emotional goal groundwork for cognitive techniques.
595.trigger: When the client appears low upon entering the room, speaking slowly, sighing; or self-reports 'not in a good mood'; obvious nonverbal tension signs.

596.skill_name: Guiding percentage rating of emotional intensity
596.skill_description: Asks the client to score the intensity of a specific emotion on a scale of 0-100%, forming quantifiable baseline data, facilitating parallel evaluation and comparison with the degree of belief in the automatic thought.
596.when_to_use: After the core emotion is determined; establishing a baseline before prosecution-defense, possibility-region and other Interventions; when needing quantitative monitoring of changes.
596.trigger: When the client has already clearly named such as 'tension/Anxiety/Depression'; the point when they can cooperate with rating their belief in Automatic thoughts.

597.skill_name: Re-evaluating emotions after Intervention and feeding back changes
597.skill_description: After completing one round of cognitive Intervention, having the client assess emotional intensity again in percentages, comparing scores before and after, and Reinforcing their awareness and improvement experience with brief feedback, consolidating change motivation.
597.when_to_use: After completing the prosecution-defense, divergent thinking, or possibility-zone discussion; at a stage summary; when improvement needs to be consolidated and new goals set.
597.trigger: A baseline score has been recorded; the client reports 'a bit better / more relaxed'; or a score decrease appears that can be compared.

598.skill_name: Comparing beliefs' emotional impact with cost-benefit Questioning
598.skill_description: Around old beliefs and alternative thoughts, separately asking 'what impacts it brings', guiding the client to compare the different consequences of the two beliefs on Anxiety/tension, using emotional benefits as the basis to facilitate choosing new thinking.
