889.when_to_use: When the key intermediate belief has been distilled after review of a negative event, or after preliminary rating, when the belief is rigid and its content and rationality need further assessment.
889.trigger: When the client is highly convinced of the belief but evidence is vague or one-sided, unable to propose evidence or ignoring other reasons, only insisting on a single Interpretation.

839.skill_name: Quantify with a ruler scale and re-measure belief conviction
839.skill_description: Based on the dialogue, directly ask the client about their degree of belief in a belief, quantify with a 1~10 scale or 0–100% to form a baseline; re-test immediately after completing evidence review or worst/best/most-realistic outcome discussion, record the change from high to low, for comparing and evaluating Intervention effectiveness.
839.when_to_use: After identifying intermediate or core negative beliefs, entering the cognitive restructuring or assessment phase, or used before and after technical intervention for comparison and monitoring change.
839.trigger: When absolute self-evaluations or rule-style beliefs appear (such as 'I am very incompetent' or 'I cannot let my parents down'), or deeply rooted negative beliefs are explicitly stated accompanied by strong emotional reactions and high certainty.

864.skill_name: Provide self-regulation strategies to support homework execution
864.skill_description: When assigning homework, simultaneously provide Coping strategies: if emotions become uncomfortable during writing or practice, remind to use the relaxation methods practiced earlier, and to dialogue with one's own emotions; normally record methods that improve emotions, to reduce physical and emotional discomfort, ensuring the homework process is safe and sustainable, and providing material for subsequent discussion.
864.when_to_use: When assigning homework or at the end of a session anticipating homework may trigger obvious emotional fluctuations; after identifying irrational beliefs, when translating ABC concepts into daily practice.
864.trigger: When the client worries homework will trigger pain or has already shown tension and discomfort in the session; reporting emotions that easily recur, overwhelming when things happen and unable to handle, lacking practice and settled methods.

1005.skill_name: Assign and schedule daily relaxation-training practice
1005.skill_description: After teaching or demonstrating Relaxation training, clearly include 'practice relaxation' in Homework, explaining practice goals and frequency, encouraging active application in real-life situations and when emotions are prone to losing control, to relieve Anxiety, irritability and poor sleep, improving self-regulation and consolidating counseling effectiveness.
1005.when_to_use: At the end of the session after teaching or demonstrating relaxation techniques, or when there is obvious Anxiety needing relief, as homework assignment for between-session consolidation and application.
1005.trigger: When the client is emotionally sensitive, anxious or sleeping poorly; Anxiety from setbacks; has learned basic relaxation techniques and needs to take them home for practice.

1146.skill_name: Assigning emotion-event and automatic-thought recording homework
1146.skill_description: Require the client to replay or recall distressing situations (including childhood memories), recording thoughts, bodily reactions and emotional changes at the time; can record triggering event A, uncomfortable emotions and behavioral consequence C and related belief B per ABC, or daily record emotions and causes, thoughts and behaviors in irritability events, for self-monitoring and subsequent analysis.
1146.when_to_use: At the end of the first or an early session, after assessment and initial diagnosis are completed; at the close of the session, assign the first round of monitoring homework; after introducing and demonstrating the ABC model, use it for consolidation.
1146.trigger: When there is pre-exam Anxiety or frequent emotional fluctuations with difficulty noticing current thoughts and reactions; in the past month there have been Anxiety, low mood, insomnia and other distresses but lacking systematic records; willing to recall and write key events.

926.skill_name: Assigning automatic-thought recording and cognitive restructuring practice
926.skill_description: Guide the client, when negative thoughts appear, to pause, examine 'whether it is reasonable, whether there are other explanations', write down the original and alternative thoughts and compare them; according to the thought record / thought change record form, continuously record events, automatic thoughts, emotions and supporting/refuting evidence, covering academic and romantic situations, as routine inter-session homework to consolidate cognitive restructuring.
926.when_to_use: At the end of the session when teaching cognitive restructuring; post-session practice during the Automatic thoughts identification and challenge phase; continuously assigned in the later consolidation phase or after the 2nd-3rd session.
926.trigger: When Automatic thoughts are frequent (such as inferiority, incompetence) and can complete written comparisons in session; already familiar with the Thought record sheet;entrenched Automatic thoughts need testing and correction.

962.skill_name: Clarifying and assigning homework at session end
962.skill_description: At the end of each counseling session, clarify this week's homework, combined with that session's discussion key points and real needs, designate concrete practice tasks (such as the three-column form, five-column form and behavioral coping training), explain the goals and methods, encourage proactively practicing and applying what was learned in real-life situations, turning the session content into after-session practice.
962.when_to_use: At the end stage of each session, when this session's gains need converting into after-session practice.
962.trigger: This technique has been explained or practiced, the core theme and goals are clear; the client has understood the related concepts/techniques and indicates they can try after-class practice.

852.skill_name: Setting homework checks and follow-up arrangements
852.skill_description: When assigning homework, specify that completion will be checked next time, and agree on the sharing method and time; at the next session, follow up on the degree of execution, giving encouragement and adjustment according to changes in adherence; at the ending stage, check and briefly discuss the records and practice materials, reinforce the effective practices, and help the client transition from passive execution to proactive completion and maintenance of the improved behavior.
852.when_to_use: At the closing segment of each session in a course of consecutive sessions; when assigning homework, simultaneously explain the checking arrangements; or before the end of each session when homework needs review.
852.trigger: When the client's homework completion is unstable; has accepted homework arrangements and needs a fixed practice and feedback rhythm; bringing or verbally reporting homework records and practice experiences.

1089.skill_name: Schedule daily relaxation practice and record effects
1089.skill_description: After guiding Relaxation training, include daily practice (such as breathing/muscle relaxation) in Homework, emphasizing practicing from the counseling room to daily life, the importance of repeated practice; require recording subjective feelings, progress and effects after each practice (can use a daily table with parental supervision), to reduce Anxiety and bodily tension, improve sleep, and provide a basis for next-time review and adjustment.
1089.when_to_use: At the end of the session after relaxation training has been demonstrated or taught, assigned as daily practice; or when confirming homework details needs to concretize frequency and implement it into daily arrangements.
1089.trigger: When the client shows Anxiety, nervousness, Difficulty falling asleep and other psychosomatic reactions and is willing to practice; has practiced relaxation in the counseling room but has not yet formed a daily plan.

1133.skill_description: Introduce and assign the recording homework: record according to the concrete daily situation, the automatic thoughts and emotional intensity at the time, adding reasonable responses and the emotional results after responding, with percentage scoring; encourage precise recording at the very moment a conflict occurs, supervised by parents when necessary, to enhance grasp of the situation-emotion-thought chain and serve as material for subsequent intervention.
1133.when_to_use: In the early 1~3 sessions or phases needing systematic practice, clarify homework and methods before the session ends; after sessions addressing Automatic thoughts or when interpersonal conflicts need improvement during the cognitive Intervention phase.
1133.trigger: The client finds it hard to notice the relationship between automatic thoughts and emotions, emotional distress repeats; interpersonal conflicts appear and recalling details is difficult; has understood the cognitive path and is willing to cooperate with self-recording.

1087.skill_name: Assign homework on irrational belief identification and cause analysis
1087.skill_description: Require systematically sorting irrational beliefs and their resulting emotional and behavioral outcomes, writing consequence C and thought B around experienced event A, analyzing the irrational components in B; recording related evidence and budding alternative thoughts, and sorting and analyzing other conflict-triggering events, providing materials and problem context for next discussion and debate correction.
1087.when_to_use: Before the session ends, after completing ABC psychoeducation or irrational belief identification, as cognitive preparation homework.
1087.trigger: When multiple irrational beliefs have been identified (such as absolutization, catastrophizing), the client can recall personal events and is willing to continue exploring; emotional improvement is limited and the framework needs consolidation.

892.skill_name: Assign homework on irrational belief debate and consolidation practice
892.skill_description: After the session, arrange written debate on irrational beliefs (such as writing >=500 words weekly), and list original irrational beliefs and newly built rational beliefs pairwise for comparison; complete a rational self-analysis report, give timely feedback on completion, continue Reflection and consolidate alternative beliefs, to promote internalization and generalization.
892.when_to_use: During the insight and working-through phase or after sessions completing irrational belief debate techniques, for consolidation and systematic practice.
892.trigger: When the client can identify or debate some irrational beliefs in session and is willing to practice correction; alternative beliefs have formed but stability is insufficient.

1011.skill_name: Teaching and assigning thought-record / three-column-form practice
1011.skill_description: Conduct psychoeducation and demonstration, explaining the CBT cognitive model and Thought record sheet filling method; require using the Thought record sheet/three-column/five-column table to record events, Automatic thoughts, supporting and opposing evidence and emotion ratings when mood changes or worsens, practice self-refutation and re-evaluation, as weekly Homework to bring back for discussion and correction.
1011.when_to_use: After completing CBT principle explanation and demonstration, assign specific practice before the session ends; assigned as between-session practice in the 2nd-3rd session or the Automatic thoughts identification and evaluation phase.
1011.trigger: When negative Automatic thoughts appear and the basic use of record forms has been learned; can preliminarily identify emotions and Automatic thoughts and is willing to practice; evidence testing is needed.

860.skill_name: Assigning daily breathing-relaxation practice and application scenarios
860.skill_description: Explain the goal is to improve sleep and Anxiety, specify practicing diaphragmatic/slow deep breathing and whole-body muscle relaxation before bed and in situations of high stress, insomnia, difficulty concentrating, Fear or palpitations; require daily practice and record completion and emotional changes, feedback effects in the next Session, to gradually form a self-help regulation skill that can be quickly applied when needed.
860.when_to_use: After teaching breathing relaxation techniques, assign it as Homework before the session ends; during the assessment and relationship-building phase or at the end of the 3rd-5th session when sleep and Anxiety-related somatic symptoms exist.
860.trigger: In the past month, cannot sleep, waking easily, tension and other symptoms; high stress, intermittent insomnia, inability to concentrate or frequent Fear/tension; already learned the basic methods in the session and responded Good.

853.skill_name: Administer and interpret SCL-90/SAS/SDS to quantify mood
853.skill_description: During the initial visit and phased assessment, administer and interpret Scale such as SCL-90, SAS, SDS, quantifying Anxiety, depression and overall symptom levels, recording scores and standard scores and comparing with previous or norm; when necessary combine with clinical interview and DSM-5 screening, forming an objective baseline and preliminary judgment, assisting subsequent Intervention and efficacy evaluation.
853.when_to_use: Used in initial assessment or at the start of a session when emotional severity needs to be quickly grasped, or at key nodes such as phased re-evaluation and case-closing follow-up.
853.trigger: When the client reports Anxiety/depression, Sleep disturbed, functional decline and other distresses; or objective quantification and before-after comparison are needed.

1191.skill_name: Use SAS/SDS to assess and give feedback with phased comparison
1191.skill_description: In counseling, administer the SAS, SDSScale to quantify Anxiety and depression levels, record standard scores and give feedback and Interpretation to the client; re-test in subsequent sessions and compare changes, to judge mood improvement and counseling efficacy, as a basis for discussion and plan adjustment.
1191.when_to_use: When initial diagnosis needs to quantify emotional severity; during phased or pre-termination assessment of Intervention effectiveness.
1191.trigger: When the client self-reports tension and unease, restlessness, persistent insomnia or obvious emotional and behavioral changes; or objective comparison with previous results is needed.

961.skill_name: Guides self-rating and collects others' feedback to assess mood trends
961.skill_description: Invite the client to self-rate the current intensity of negative emotion with a score and compare it with the established goal or the previous score; simultaneously collect observations from peers and others and the client's subjective self-report, re-measure the scales and comprehensively judge mood changes and efficacy, enhancing the reliability and ecological validity of the assessment.
961.when_to_use: At periodic assessment or session summary, when the degree of emotional improvement and goal attainment needs to be judged; during follow-up, when scale changes and functional improvement need verification.
961.trigger: The client mentions mood fluctuations, improvement/worsening of the chief complaint, or a need to review progress and evaluate effects.

1009.skill_name: Observe and use structured inquiry to comprehensively assess current mood
1009.skill_description: At the start of the session, observe nonverbal cues such as demeanor, emotions and tone, and conduct structured inquiry and recording around insomnia, Anxiety, tearfulness, etc.; combine chief complaints, others' accounts and functional impairment, clarify current main emotions and their impact, forming a comprehensive judgment of current mood and risk.
1009.when_to_use: At the state assessment and symptom tracking at the start of each session, or when mood and symptom data need to be updated.
1009.trigger: When the client appears tense and uneasy, Low mood or self-reports emotional distress in the past two weeks, with sleep/study functioning affected; Teacher or family provides information on recent changes.

844.skill_name: Conducts a mood score check and names the emotion in each session
844.skill_description: At the session opening, conduct a mood check, inviting the client to review feelings of the past week or recent period, use 0–10 or score-based self-rating of tension/Anxiety intensity, record the values and compare changes later, while providing emotion-word options to help them Naming emotions, quickly grasping the current baseline and fluctuations.
844.when_to_use: At the beginning of each session, used to quickly understand the current mood and establish or update a common reference.
844.trigger: A new week's session begins, or the client expresses their current mood vaguely and reports emotional ups and downs, needing scores and emotion words to describe the state.

931.skill_name: Explains the assessment reasons and administers core scales to establish a baseline
931.skill_description: After explaining the assessment reasons to the client and obtaining consent, administer core Scale such as SCL-90, SDS, SAS and SBQ-R, quantifying depression, Anxiety and suicide risk, obtaining a baseline and re-testing in subsequent phases to monitor changes, providing a basis for referral and Intervention decisions.
931.when_to_use: During the initial assessment phase and when efficacy or risk changes need monitoring, especially when self-injury risk or emotional distress is significant.
931.trigger: When the client has recent self-injury/suicide ideation, self-reports Low mood and worsened Anxiety, or before collaborating with psychiatry to develop a plan.

1088.skill_name: At the opening, describing and rating current emotions, observing and clarifying reactions
1088.skill_description: At the start of the session, guide the client to describe recent stress, Anxiety and low mood and other emotional reactions, giving normalized understanding; guide them to grade pain intensity and match Coping skills accordingly; combine on-site nonverbal and verbal cues to collect mood information, recalling and recording the past month's emotions and thoughts when necessary, openly inquiring about triggers and changes, clarifying emotional reactions around event details.
1088.when_to_use: At the opening of the 2nd and subsequent sessions, when the client's mood and stress state need to be understood, or before entering the topic/cognitive processing, when a baseline of current emotion needs to be quickly established.
1088.trigger: When the client pours out real-life difficulties and emotional distress, showing obvious emotional reactions or pauses and sighs; saying 'does not know how to handle such thoughts'.

1078.skill_name: Guide 0–10/0–100 self-rating of Anxiety with before-after comparison tracking
1078.skill_description: Guide the client to use a numeric Scale to immediately assess current Anxiety/tension intensity (such as 0–10 or 0–100), record the score and continuously compare across sessions, as a simple indicator for quickly grasping mood fluctuations and Intervention effectiveness; can score specific situations to monitor trends.
1078.when_to_use: At the opening stage of the session, to quickly grasp the mood, or when formulating/following up behavior plans and reviewing changes at the ending stage.
1078.trigger: When signs of tension like sweaty palms appear or the client self-reports Anxiety, reporting emotional fluctuations, needing immediate assessment and comparison with previous ratings.

1143.skill_name: Administer AnxietyScale for phased assessment and compare changes
1143.skill_description: In the first session, administer AnxietyScale such as SAS, and re-administer later (such as the exam AnxietyScale), quantifying current Anxiety levels and change trends, recording scores and conducting phased comparisons, providing a basis for Intervention and effect evaluation.
1143.when_to_use: First session and phased assessment; at the start of each session when Anxiety levels need to be understood or re-testing after Intervention.
1143.trigger: When the client reports Anxiety fluctuations, sleep or functional changes, or quantitative assessment of phased effectiveness is needed.

1071.skill_name: Observe nonverbal and behavioral cues to quickly assess mood
1071.skill_description: Notice nonverbal and verbal cues such as facial expressions, posture, tone, speech rate, tearing, like worried faces, restlessness, repeated small movements, comprehensively judging current mood and pain levels; and cross-validating with Scale and self-reports, as a basis for immediate emotion assessment.
1071.when_to_use: Quick emotional scan at the start of each session, or when Scale is not available; when emotional fluctuations are obvious during narration.
1071.trigger: Observable signals appear, such as a haggard face, lowered head, low tone, repeated sighing, avoiding eye contact, tearful complaints.

967.skill_name: Administering SCL-90/SAS/SDS to establish a mood baseline and compare before and after
967.skill_description: In the first or assessment phase, use SCL-90, SAS, SDS for assessment, recording total scores, factor scores and standard scores, quantifying depression, Anxiety and overall symptom levels; re-test at termination or key milestones and compare with pre-tests, judging mood changes and counseling efficacy, as a basis for diagnosis and goal setting.
967.when_to_use: Used at the first interview or diagnostic assessment stage when a preliminary psychological assessment is needed; at ending or phased assessment when change needs quantifying.
967.trigger: When the client comes for the first session or self-reports Low mood, Anxiety, insomnia, interpersonal sensitivity and other distresses, needing objective severity determination and before-after comparison.

1066.skill_name: Use 0–10/0–100 emotion scale to assess intensity and track
1066.skill_description: Guide the client to score negative emotions of the moment such as panic, nervousness, anger, and sadness using a 0-10 or 0-100 emotion scale, record the score and compare it with the last record, quickly grasp the severity and trend, as a basis for monitoring and later intervention.
1066.when_to_use: Mood check at the start of the session, or when intensity needs to be quickly grasped after symptom fluctuation or a crisis event; after exposure practice, changes need to be compared.
1066.trigger: When the client reports Anxiety, irritability, depression and other negative emotions or has difficulty describing intensity; after completing exposure exercises.

1020.skill_name: Administering SAS/SDS with feedback and interpretation, and stage re-testing for comparison
1020.skill_description: After completing SAS/SDS assessment, give the client feedback on scores and their meaning, determining Anxiety/depression severity; re-test at initial assessment, phased and follow-up milestones and compare with baseline, objectively assessing changes and counseling effects, combining with medical diagnosis when necessary.
1020.when_to_use: Feedback and explanation are needed after testing is completed; at initial consultation and phased retesting, and when evaluating effects before termination.
1020.trigger: When Scale scoring is complete and shows Anxiety/depression or related problems; comparison with initial scores is needed to assess progress.

1154.skill_name: Clinically observing and recording emotional cues and overall impressions
1154.skill_description: During the interview, note appearance, speech, emotional expression and psychotic signs, recording Low mood, Anxiety and other cues, and combining with thought coherence, insight and guardedness for an overall impression, forming a preliminary judgment of current mood, as a basis for subsequent Intervention.
1154.when_to_use: The diagnostic assessment and rapport-building stage of the initial visit, and any point where the current emotional state needs to be grasped.
1154.trigger: When presenting tension, defensiveness, fatigue or lowness in nonverbal and verbal signals upon entering; chief complaint is poor mood but without psychotic symptoms.

916.skill_name: Use SCL-90 for initial assessment and post-test comparison to evaluate changes
916.skill_description: After explaining the assessment purpose, complete the SCL-90, recording total scores and related factor scores and comparing with norms or pre-tests, judging the severity and change trends of depression, Anxiety, interpersonal sensitivity, etc., as objective evidence of counseling effectiveness and subsequent plan adjustment.
916.when_to_use: During initial consultation or when objective quantification of current symptoms and mood is needed; during phased assessment or before termination when Intervention effectiveness needs testing.
916.trigger: The client reports a very bad mood, worries about depression, symptoms are widespread or subjective improvement/fluctuation is felt, needing quantitative monitoring.

1144.skill_name: Observe immediate emotions and nonverbal reactions under trigger topics
1144.skill_description: When discussing trigger topics like exams, notice pained expressions, tense demeanor, changes in speech rate and tone, posture, finger-biting and other nonverbal and bodily reactions, comprehensively judging the immediate intensity of Anxiety, anger, sadness and other emotions, as mood cues at the start of the session.
1144.when_to_use: At the session segment entering the topic or discussing stressful events, when the immediate emotional intensity needs to be quickly grasped.
1144.trigger: When talking about trigger topics, obvious cues appear like pained expressions, tense posture, fluctuating speech rate, not daring to make eye contact.

1180.skill_name: Open-ended inquiry about recent mood and troubles, specifying triggers
1180.skill_description: At the session opening, use open-ended Questioning to understand the overall mood of the past one to two weeks and the currently most distressing problems, further concretely inquiring about triggering events and duration, letting the client freely describe Loneliness, gloom, inferiority, Anxiety and sleep/appetite changes, comprehensively assessing mood and the scope and intensity of distress.
1180.when_to_use: At the mood assessment stage at the first and each session's opening, or after obtaining recent sleep information when the emotional state needs updating.
1180.trigger: When the client is willing to express distress or proactively describes recent feelings; has briefly reported life changes but emotional state and main troubles are not yet clear.

1136.skill_name: Directly ask about current suicide ideation and determine risk
1136.skill_description: In an open, non-judgmental way, directly ask whether suicide thoughts or ideation exist recently, clarifying presence/absence and intensity, frequency and most recent occurrence, as a safety screening and risk assessment basis for depression cases or those with prior suicide ideation.
1136.when_to_use: At the opening mood assessment of each session for depression cases or those with prior suicide ideation; during initial assessment or when emotions fluctuate significantly.
1136.trigger: When the client mentions lowness, despair, Death-related expressions, or records indicate a history of suicide ideation.

1010.skill_name: Comprehensively assess suicide risk and initiate Intervention when necessary
1010.skill_description: Through interviews, assess whether suicide thoughts and behaviors occurred in the past three months, understanding ideation frequency, methods and whether concretized (such as location), combining with past self-injury history and current emotional presentation to determine crisis level; even if the client self-reports no current ideation, still comprehensively assess and coordinate with the school psychological crisis Intervention when needed to ensure safety.
1010.when_to_use: At the first visit or whenever suicide ideation is found at the start of any session, safety and risk assessment should take priority; re-assess when self-injury-related information appears later.
1010.trigger: When the client states danger signals like 'living is meaningless' or 'can leave without pain soon', revealing past suicide experiences or fluctuating self-injury thoughts and behaviors.

1091.skill_name: Use SCL-90 and SAS to assess and give face-to-face feedback and interpretation
1091.skill_description: Guide the client to complete the SCL-90 and SAS tests, recording Anxiety and somatization scores, and give face-to-face feedback and Interpretation of factor scores and comparison with normal values, forming a preliminary analysis of problem severity and type, supporting subsequent counseling plans and goal setting.
1091.when_to_use: When psychological testing is conducted at the first counseling, or at the stage where a preliminary judgment of the problem's severity needs to be formed; at the start of the session when mood and symptom severity need to be understood.
1091.trigger: When first visiting or the client self-reports Anxiety, interpersonal sensitivity, somatization and other distresses, needing objective quantification of symptom levels.

1189.skill_name: Observing nonverbal and physiological signals and giving brief feedback to calibrate assessment
1189.skill_description: Combined with nonverbal and physiological signals such as the relaxation of the face and limbs, posture and speech rate, observe such things as leg shaking, hands tightly rubbing, brows tightly furrowed, shoulders and neck tense, eyes reddened, give brief feedback to calibrate and supplement the mood information of the subjective ratings, assisting the immediate judgment of tension and emotional activation levels.
1189.when_to_use: Used after mood rating to verify and enrich the emotion assessment; at the start of sessions and when talking about stressful events, to grasp the state in real time.
1189.trigger: When noticing nonverbal signals consistent or inconsistent with reported emotions, or obvious tense bodily and verbal signals appear when narrating stressful events.

1021.skill_name: Retesting SAS/SDS before the end and comparing with initial tests to assess improvement
1021.skill_description: In the termination or consolidation phase, re-administer SAS/SDS, recording standard scores and comparing with initial assessment results, objectively assessing the improvement magnitude of Anxiety and depression and counseling effectiveness, giving the client feedback on changes for case closure and consolidation planning.
1021.when_to_use: During the effect evaluation segment of the Consolidation and termination phase; review summaries of the third to sixth sessions or follow-up reviews.
1021.trigger: When preparing to end counseling or needing to evaluate the stage effect, when the pre-test was completed earlier and comparison with the baseline is needed.

1057.skill_name: Reinforce strengths and positive experiences to enhance self-efficacy
1057.skill_description: Identify and affirm the client's strengths (such as curiosity, courage, hope, self-control), reinforcing them with specific examples; guide recall of joyful events, and compare emotional and functional performance when using old vs new ideas, connecting to new choices and attempts, enhancing intrinsic motivation, self-efficacy and commitment to change.
1057.when_to_use: Before and after planning a new path, after emotional venting, or after a successful experience appears, used to consolidate motivation, maintain change, and increase engagement.
1057.trigger: When strengths are revealed in session but self-worth is underestimated; uncertain about the benefits of correcting beliefs or hesitant about trying new behaviors; Low mood, strong sense of worthlessness.

851.skill_name: Generate alternative coping and reinforce with small-step tasks
851.skill_description: Invite the client to imagine 'what to do next time', encourage proposing alternative plans (such as first controlling the emotions, discussing compensation with classmates), and assign feasible small-step tasks (such as communicating, exercising, keeping a diary, relaxation practice); give affirming feedback, letting them obtain positive experience, thereby strengthening the willingness and sense of efficacy to try new behaviors.
851.when_to_use: When motivation is activated and willing to change but not yet equipped with alternative strategies, or after cognitive discussion, when assigning homework at the end of each session, to facilitate executable plans and consolidate motivation.
851.trigger: When the client realizes old rules are unfair and is willing to try other ways; or stress, Anxiety are high, attention is scattered, doubtful about change, needing positive experience support.

1156.skill_name: Conveying external validation and affirming progress to consolidate motivation
1156.skill_description: At key points, convey positive feedback from teachers and others, clearly point out and affirm the client's progress and new understanding as positive reinforcement, prompting them to keep trying new behaviors or challenge higher goals, maintain motivation for change, and enhance self-efficacy.
1156.when_to_use: After a first attempt, before consolidating motivation or planning a higher-difficulty challenge, or when reviewing practice and at the later stage of symptom improvement, used to maintain and amplify motivation for change.
1156.trigger: The client hesitates about continuing to try and needs encouragement and affirmation; reports small improvements, completes tasks, or can state a concrete plan and increased confidence.

929.skill_name: Connecting value outcomes and developing specific follow-up behaviors
929.skill_description: Clearly propose the positive results that change may bring (such as interpersonal improvement, better sleep), invite the client to propose and refine the next actions (such as apology and communication plans), turn belief change into executable goals, raising inner motivation and responsibility, and test the new concepts in real situations.
929.when_to_use: After a technique experience or debate, when motivation is aroused, used to turn change intentions into concrete and executable follow-up plans.
929.trigger: The client hopes to improve a relationship or sleep but hesitates to act; or has expressed willingness to change/raised a preliminary intention, needing clarification and planning to promote execution.

1081.skill_name: Resource-oriented review and affirmation to enhance a sense of control
1081.skill_description: Review years of effort and ability, highlighting successful experiences and acknowledging effort, combining phased progress summaries and positive feedback, reducing the sense of incompetence, enhancing 'I can change' confidence and persistence, supporting correction of Intermediate beliefs and continued trying of new behaviors.
1081.when_to_use: When the case hesitates about change, self-rated ability is insufficient or self-evaluation is low, or at the end of training/phased counseling when motivation for continued change needs reinforcement.
1081.trigger: When 'I cannot do it/I cannot change' helpless expressions appear, showing inferiority and helplessness; or after completing exercises, reporting improved attention and reduced Anxiety needing consolidation.

1155.skill_name: Sets progressive goals and small tasks to create success experiences
1155.skill_description: Suggest formulating a detailed plan, first setting daily small goals that are easy to complete, then gradually increasing the task volume; set small, attainable exercises and review successes in time, use actual progress to counter old assumptions such as 'poor memory', and enhance the motivation to correct old beliefs and sustain action.
1155.when_to_use: When finding it hard to engage in action, seeking quick fixes with heavy Anxiety burden, or after correcting related ideas when successful experiences are needed to consolidate change and maintain action.
1155.trigger: Acknowledging past reliance on pre-exam cramming, currently finding it hard to dive into review all at once, difficulty starting; taking a wait-and-see attitude toward change or still lacking confidence in technique effectiveness.

1179.skill_name: Timely positive reinforcement and encouragement to maintain change motivation
1179.skill_description: In sessions and homework feedback, promptly express thanks, affirmation, and appreciation, point out concrete progress and strengths (such as eye contact, proactive communication), use praise and emotional support with a factual basis to consolidate reasonable beliefs and adaptive behaviors, and raise self-efficacy and the willingness to keep changing.
1179.when_to_use: After each session and homework feedback, during the Consolidation and termination phase, or when more rational expressions, new adaptive behaviors and signs of progress appear.
1179.trigger: When the client completes tasks, state improves, interpersonal interactions improve or new behavior signs are shown; when confidence in continued change is insufficient or external recognition is needed.

1176.skill_name: Affirm effort and plan a sustained practice path
1176.skill_description: At the consolidation and ending stage, summarize the results, affirm the client's investment and change, discuss how to adopt rational strategies such as rational emotive therapy, communication, and emotional expression in the future, clarify the direction of continued practice, enhance self-efficacy, and consolidate commitment to the new notions and new behaviors.
1176.when_to_use: In the Consolidation and termination segment of the 9th~10th session, or at the end of each session, to reinforce the motivation and path for continued change.
1176.trigger: The client worries about maintaining change or motivation fluctuates, and needs to be seen and encouraged and to obtain a clear continuing pathway.

875.skill_name: Consolidating progress and inspiring persistence with feedback and review
875.skill_description: Periodically review the effective methods and concrete changes (emotion, cognition, behavior, and social functioning), give qualitative/quantitative feedback and encouragement, clarify the direction for continuing or generalize rational thinking to other domains, and enhance the sense of gain and the intrinsic motivation to keep practicing.
875.when_to_use: At the end of a stage or after an important exercise is completed, or when evaluating effects in the closing stage, used to integrate gains, maintain and enhance motivation for change.
875.trigger: The client has a vague sense of benefit from counseling and questions the need to continue investing, or in the closing phase needs to consolidate confidence and a continuous action plan.

1167.skill_name: Compare irrational and rational beliefs with a pros-cons list
1167.skill_description: Jointly sort out the emotional and life costs caused by irrational beliefs, and compare the positive effects brought by rational beliefs, clarifying their links with Anxiety, insomnia, Decreased efficiency and other consequences, forming a pros-cons checklist or comparison table homework, highlighting the drawbacks of old strategies and consolidating the sense of gain from new thinking.
1167.when_to_use: After identifying and preliminarily substituting, after preliminary practice or when motivation is insufficient and wavering, used to enhance willingness and persistence to change.
1167.trigger: When the client wavers, returns to old thinking or thinks change is not very meaningful; insufficient understanding of change benefits; persistent anxiety that has not yet been linked with irrational beliefs; thinking old ideas are safer.

1033.skill_name: Present the real costs of old beliefs and old strategies
1033.skill_description: Through benefit-cost analysis and consequence questioning, point out the costs of persisting with old beliefs and old coping (such as limited job search scope, damaged relationships, Anxiety and Increased stress), focusing on current and future adverse consequences, shaking the appeal of old ideas, enhancing motivation to correct and try new behaviors.
1033.when_to_use: During the motivational interviewing phase or when starting belief change; when willingness to change is insufficient, old strategies are idealized or focusing on real costs is needed.
1033.trigger: The client clings to old concepts and defends themself on the grounds of 'at least it can make me feel better'; emphasizes the benefits of the old concepts while ignoring consequences; mainly avoids and ingratiates yet admits real harm.

1055.skill_name: Debate with irrational beliefs to promote correction
1055.skill_description: Conduct rational debate around key irrational beliefs, examining evidence and logic, proposing exception scenarios and alternative views, and pointing out the negative cycle maintaining old ideas, letting the client experience the emotional and behavioral improvements brought by rational beliefs, enhancing change motivation and action readiness.
1055.when_to_use: After identifying key irrational ideas, in the second phase/working-through phase or after completing psychoeducation and entering the belief correction and motivation arousal phase, use.
1055.trigger: When absolute, should-style or rigid beliefs appear accompanied by Anxiety, Relationship tension; or though theory is understood, old ideas are still held, with emotions and behaviors not yet obviously improved.

1018.skill_name: Weigh the short-term gains and long-term costs of avoidance
1018.skill_description: Guide distinguishing the immediate relief of avoidance from long-term consequences (Loneliness, maintaining Anxiety, weakening sense of control and self-efficacy, hindering belief correction), list the roles of procrastination, phone-scrolling, deep breathing in the cycle, highlighting that old strategies do more harm than good, prompting them to stop Withdrawal and try new behaviors.
1018.when_to_use: When motivation is weak or avoidance persists, or during exposure planning and motivation enhancement, used to clarify the meaning of giving up safety behaviors and enhance willingness to try.
1018.trigger: Acknowledging avoidance brings comfort but not yet realizing long-term impacts; expressing avoidance tendencies like 'waiting to be automatically laid off' or 'doing nothing at all now'; defending avoidance like 'not looking at the phone makes me more anxious'.

1001.skill_name: Build an Anxiety situation hierarchy and starting tasks
1001.skill_description: Collaborate with the client and parents to list all feared or Anxiety-inducing events, grade them by 0~100 or 1—6 subjective Anxiety levels, arrange typical situations from low to high, prioritizing low-risk, controllable starting tasks, forming an executable practice checklist and exposure sequence, preparing for subsequent trials.
1001.when_to_use: In the planning stage before behavioral experiments/exposure, before the first implementation, when practice goals and difficulty gradients need to be clarified.
1001.trigger: When the client describes multiple avoidance or tension scenarios with varying intensity; willing to try but Anxiety is high, or hesitant about directly entering high-difficulty situations and worried about failure.

948.skill_name: Implement behavioral experiments in levels and assess escalation
948.skill_description: Based on the constructed Anxiety hierarchy, start from low to medium difficulty, first desensitize in imagination, then gradually try in reality by situation (such as bus, park, mall, provincial capital, high-speed rail); after completing each phase goal, assess the Anxiety score, entering a higher level when below 40 or no longer obviously anxious, using actual results to test and correct catastrophizing beliefs and avoidance behaviors.
948.when_to_use: When conducting or advancing graded behavioral experiments and exposure, when practice needs to be promoted across multiple situations, catastrophic beliefs verified, and excessive challenge avoided.
948.trigger: When single exposure is effective but generalization is insufficient; directly challenging too high leads to retreat; listing multiple Fear scenarios with long-term avoidance of going out or riding; avoiding specific situations like employment, postgraduate-exam exchanges, sharing inner thoughts, with significant Anxiety.

1072.skill_description: Explain in plain language A (event) - B (belief) - C (emotion/behavior) and the ABCDE framework, demonstrate the causal chain 'event - thought - emotion', emphasize that distress is mostly determined by beliefs and that beliefs can be tested and revised; when necessary invite the client to restate it in their own words, building a shared language and a sense that change is feasible.
1072.when_to_use: The psychoeducation stage at the start of treatment or before each entry into cognitive / debate work, used to establish a shared understanding and a path of change.
1072.trigger: The client attributes emotions entirely to external events, or feels confused or skeptical about 'beliefs affecting emotions / whether change is possible', or proactively asks about the principles of the method.

915.skill_name: Clarify that beliefs are changeable and the rational-testing path
915.skill_description: Clarify that irrational beliefs are not fixed, and can be clarified and corrected through Confrontation, analysis, evidence testing and rational debate, gradually establishing more reasonable thinking patterns, enhancing changeability cognition and self-efficacy, laying the foundation for subsequent debate and practice.
915.when_to_use: In the educational segment before starting cognitive restructuring or during phased summaries, used to reinforce 'beliefs can change' and specific change paths; when the client doubts whether change is possible or lacks a sense of method.
915.trigger: When the client says 'I am just like this' or 'cannot change', or does not know how to change, feeling helpless and doubtful about effectiveness and methods.

895.skill_name: Model rational alternatives and arrange consolidation practice
895.skill_description: Demonstrate replacing old ideas with more realistic rational statements (such as 'everyone has strengths and weaknesses' or 'many people like me'), explaining 'when thinking changes, emotions change accordingly', and agree to spend about 5 minutes daily reviewing and consolidating new beliefs, improving acceptance and execution.
895.when_to_use: After identifying key irrational beliefs, when preparing to develop alternatives, or when the client is willing to try different views but doubts effectiveness and methods.
895.trigger: When the client acknowledges old beliefs bring pain, expressions like 'maybe my personality is too weird/not worthy of being liked' appear, willing to try but hesitant.

907.skill_name: Using cases to explain ABC and distinguish events from beliefs
907.skill_description: Explain A (event)–B (belief)–C (emotion/behavior) in plain language, giving on-the-spot examples from their current situation and distinguishing A, B, C, clarifying that distress stems from beliefs rather than events; when necessary introduce common features of irrational beliefs, establishing the cognitive framework and common language of 'changing beliefs can change outcomes'.
907.when_to_use: During psychoeducation and insight phases, before entering cognitive Intervention or when the client is eager to relieve emotions but unclear about principles.
907.trigger: The client insists 'it was the event that made me like this', attributes emotions entirely to external causes, or feels confused or curious about the principles of the counseling method and the path of change.

1113.skill_name: Explain three types of irrational beliefs with case comparison
1113.skill_description: Explain the definitions and manifestations of three types of irrational beliefs: absolute Demands, overgeneralization, terrible, combining the client's original words and situations item by item, helping them identify clues in daily conversation, enhancing self-recognition and correction awareness.
1113.when_to_use: After the ABC framework is established, preparing to identify specific deviation types of item B or entering the cognitive education phase before debate.
1113.trigger: When the client frequently uses extreme statements like 'should/must' or 'worthless/certainly......' feeling confused about the concept and types of 'irrational beliefs'.

1082.skill_name: Use downward-arrow to probe layer by layer to the core belief
1082.skill_description: Around Automatic thoughts in prominent emotions or key situations, repeatedly asking 'what does this mean/what is the worst that could happen', continuously clarifying their meaning and consequences, probing layer by layer until fundamental judgments about self, others or the world emerge (such as 'I am very incompetent/the world is dangerous'), and connecting surface thoughts with deep beliefs, referencing early experience clues when necessary to deepen identification.
1082.when_to_use: When emotions are intense or a key theme appears and only surface automatic thoughts are obtained; or when entering longitudinal/case conceptualization and core-belief work, needing to clarify the belief hierarchy from surface to depth.
1082.trigger: When the client stays at surface thoughts after specific events (such as 'cannot learn well'), accompanied by Shame, guilt, anxiety and physiological reactions; or repeatedly showing self-blame, ability evaluation and fixed reaction patterns, confused about the source and willing to explore further.

843.skill_name: Combine Socratic Questioning to probe down to core beliefs
843.skill_description: Capture key Automatic thoughts (such as 'I get nervous' or 'others will think I am strange'), using Socratic questioning with the downward arrow repeatedly asking 'what does this mean/what is the worst that could happen', gradually connecting attitude rules and early experiences, until distilling core beliefs like 'I am not worthy of being loved/the surroundings are not safe/I am abandoned'.
843.when_to_use: After identifying negative Automatic thoughts, when needing to go deeper to the intermediate/core belief stage; or when needing to quickly reach root beliefs from surface thoughts in specific interpersonal/Anxiety situations.
843.trigger: When the client has strong emotions in interpersonal situations, rigid Interpretation, or self-states 'not worthy of being loved'; surface thoughts like 'they are all watching me' or 'will speak incoherently in public' appear in records or dialogue, highly sensitive to others' evaluation and willing to accept further questioning.

1119.skill_name: Generate multiple explanations and coping options from a shifted perspective
1119.skill_description: When information is vague or others' intentions are unclear, guide the client to compare others'/peers' different reactions to the same event, using perspective-shifting Questioning (such as from the other party's, family's, friend's standpoint) to propose more than one possible Interpretation, and expand with own experience and situational clues; when necessary also discuss more appropriate handling or alternative paths, to break single negative attributions, broaden cognitive perspective, relieve Anxiety and self-blame.
1119.when_to_use: When the client forms a single negative interpretation of social / work / family situations, when automatic thoughts are evaluated, or when understanding and action options need to be broadened.
1119.trigger: Insisting on 'only one reason/conclusion' (such as 'they certainly do not like me' or 'I am stupid'), showing absolute attribution, mind-reading inference or self-blaming Interpretation, thus hesitating and avoiding, with actions blocked.

1014.skill_name: Check evidence and assess each explanation's credibility
1014.skill_description: After multiple possible explanations have been proposed, urge the client to find real-life grounds and counter-evidence for each explanation, conduct a preliminary check based on known facts and the person's own statements, write them into the thought record form when necessary and mark the belief percentage, discuss their reasonableness item by item, to reduce the emotional distress caused by overgeneralization and single negative attribution.
1014.when_to_use: After identifying Automatic thoughts or generating several alternative Interpretations, when needing to check evidence and estimate the reasonableness and relative likelihood of each Interpretation.
1014.trigger: The client always thinks the worst, repeatedly dwells on the meanings of others' words; or interprets events only as 'being abandoned/deliberately making things difficult' as the sole conclusion, ignoring other possibilities.

996.skill_name: Explain attribution differences and guide alternative explanations
996.skill_description: Through examples illustrating the subjective experience differences brought by different attribution styles, prompting possible cognitive biases; in role reversal or when discussing conflict segments, use prompts like 'what do you think she wants to express' to encourage the client to organize narratives from others' intentions and feelings, opening multi-angle thinking, expanding multiple Interpretations of events.
996.when_to_use: When the client forms a single explanation of an event and has difficulty seeing other possibilities; or during role reversal and replaying peak-conflict segments to activate the other's perspective.
996.trigger: Persistently attributes events such as breakups unidirectionally to the other party or the outside; falls into self-centered narration, silence, or hesitation, finding it hard to unfold others' perspectives.

1003.skill_name: Planning coping based on alternative explanations and projecting outcomes
1003.skill_description: After generating multiple reasonable Interpretations, guide matching each possibility with coping options (such as communicating to explain or shifting focus to studies/trying other companies), referring to peer experiences to preliminarily estimate feasibility, and deducing the choices and possible feelings when adopting different Interpretations at present, thereby relieving catastrophizing, supporting decision-making and action.
1003.when_to_use: When multiple alternative Interpretations have been diverged, hoping to further connect to specific behavioral choices and emotional change, or when the client equates a single event with the only terrible outcome, needing to expand possibilities to reduce Anxiety.
1003.trigger: Expressing catastrophic conclusions like 'if the company does not keep me = no way out' or 'only terrible endings'; or having listed 2–3 possibilities but staying at the abstract level, not yet linked to concrete consequences.

1044.skill_name: Building and rating a graded exposure list
1044.skill_description: Jointly list specific situations prone to triggering Anxiety/compulsion with the client, scoring each by subjective difficulty or Fear/Anxiety intensity (such as 0–10) and sorting from low to high, forming a graded task/situation table, providing a progressively advancing execution framework for subsequent behavioral experiments, in-vivo exposure and response prevention, reducing failure risk and gradually accumulating successful experiences.
1044.when_to_use: Used in the planning stage before implementing exposure / behavioral experiments, to clarify the target situation, difficulty, and progression order.
1044.trigger: When the client can identify Anxiety/compulsion-triggering scenarios but finds it hard to directly enter high-difficulty tasks, or needs to distinguish the Anxiety intensity and practice order of different situations.

901.skill_name: Negotiate the starting level of the first exposure
901.skill_description: After completing the situation list and level ratings, negotiate with the client to determine the starting level for first exposure, prioritizing tolerable low-to-medium difficulty as the starting point, ensuring safety and control, lowering the entry threshold, and improving participation and persistence.
901.when_to_use: In the task-selection segment before carrying out exposure/behavioral experiments, when the starting difficulty and method need to be determined.
901.trigger: After the situations and ratings are completed, the client expresses the tolerability of each level; or fears high-difficulty situations but is willing to try lower-difficulty practice.

1097.skill_name: Repeat exposure assessment and advance per criteria
1097.skill_description: In the same-level situations, arrange repeated exposure and practice, which can be combined with deep breathing/muscle relaxation to relieve tension; assess subjective Anxiety after each (such as 0–10 or Scale scores), entering a higher level when reduced to about half of the initial, below 3 or below 40 points; if not yet meeting the standard, continue practicing or adjust, avoiding skipping levels, steadily consolidating new coping in a safe, relaxed environment.
1097.when_to_use: After establishing the hierarchy and completing low-level training, or at the end of each stage of practice, when the effect needs to be evaluated and a decision made on whether to upgrade.
1097.trigger: When Anxiety at the current level has decreased significantly/scores near half of the initial, dropped below 3 or below 40 points; the client can stably tolerate and is willing to advance; or bodily reactions like tension appear during exposure needing relaxation support.

881.skill_name: Engage in active social practice to test interpersonal cognitions
881.skill_description: Under the counselor's guidance, arrange small-step real-life practice, such as proactively greeting in class/dormitory, communicating with classmates or approaching like-minded peers, increasing the frequency and depth of interaction, collecting feedback on others' responses and one's own emotional changes, to verify the worry of 'being gossiped about/discriminated against' and the possibility of being accepted, gradually enhancing social support and the sense of belonging.
881.when_to_use: In the working-through and ending consolidation stage, or when in a new environment longing for friendship, when reasonable cognition and awareness of one's own strengths need to be transformed into concrete interaction behaviors, advancing interpersonal improvement.
881.trigger: When the client Feels isolated, lacks confidence or worries about being talked about, but is willing to try proactive contact; hoping to improve dorm/classmate relationships, expand the support circle or observe interpersonal and emotional changes in practice.

1002.skill_name: Build and score the Anxiety/Fear event hierarchy table
1002.skill_description: With the client (jointly with family when necessary), sort out specific events triggering tension, fear or Anxiety, mark them by subjective intensity with 0–100 or graded methods and sort from weak to strong (such as 10 levels or 1—6 levels), clarifying practice priorities and target difficulty, providing a basis and starting point for Systematic desensitization and real-world practice.
1002.when_to_use: In the preparation phase before conducting Systematic desensitization or behavioral practice, when target situations, intensity and practice order need to be clarified.
1002.trigger: When the client has difficulty identifying the most feared scenario or practice priorities are unclear; tension levels differ markedly across situations, needing a graded plan.

976.skill_name: Set stage goals and practice gradually by hierarchy
976.skill_description: Based on the established 1—6 level or ten-level Anxiety hierarchy, set phased goals achievable through own effort for each level; practice gradually from low to high against corresponding specific events, progressively increasing difficulty to promote desensitization.
976.when_to_use: After the grading is completed, entering the beginning and implementation stage of each level of training, when the goal of that practice needs to be clarified and the actual practice carried out.
976.trigger: The hierarchy table has been completed, actual practice needs to be entered and this stage's goals clarified; or difficulty needs to be gradually increased according to an established order.

1120.skill_name: Externalize and name old core beliefs and their impact
1120.skill_description: Help the client distill the old belief in their own words, invite the voice of the old belief and the wounded experiences to be expressed; clarify the core sentence pattern and the emotional and behavioral consequences it brings, making it the standpoint and arguments of one side of the dialogue, paving the way for later refutation and substitution.
1120.when_to_use: When entering core belief evaluation, before entering the belief dialogue, or at the confrontation preparation stage, when the old belief needs to be focused on and its scope of influence clarified.
1120.trigger: When the client repeatedly Self-denial, binding results with self-worth; self-reporting absolute thoughts like 'letting others down' or 'not being loved' and feeling significantly distressed; or starting to be willing to pour out hurt experiences and worries.

1041.skill_name: Build and verbalize new beliefs responding to old ones
1041.skill_description: Guide forming more realistic, supportive self-statements, use first-person positive sentence forms to respond item by item to the old beliefs, compare with the contrast list the two's impact on emotions and behavior; combined with current positive experiences and situational evidence record and review, prompt acting according to the new beliefs, raise the degree of belief and solidify them into a repeatable script.
1041.when_to_use: In counseling dialogue or homework review, the client has already shown more realistic views and is willing to explore alternative beliefs, or in the later stage of belief work and the closing consolidation stage when the stability of the new belief needs to be raised.
1041.trigger: When Self-denial expressions or ignoring successful experiences appear; old thoughts recur (such as 'I am stupid') and wavering between new and old expressions; or new cognitive signs like 'lowering expectations' or 'seeing problems from multiple angles' have appeared.

878.skill_name: Guide self-dialogue from the future self and friend perspectives
878.skill_description: Have the client, through oral or written expression as 'the future confident self', present views and encouragement to 'the current self', or convert the reasonable comfort they would give friends into supportive words for themselves, facilitating inner dialogue between the supportive 'new self' and critical 'old self', supporting new beliefs with new experiences, correcting old Interpretations.
878.when_to_use: At the consolidation or core-belief evaluation stage, when the persuasiveness of the new belief needs to be enhanced and the change consolidated, or when the client has difficulty generating alternative thoughts and a gentler and more supportive self-voice needs to be introduced.
878.trigger: When the client reports feeling fulfilled, accomplished and expresses willingness to end counseling; or can give reasonable advice to others but is harsh on themselves, with negative Automatic thoughts like 'they deliberately do not respond to me'.

1149.skill_name: Summarizing new explanations and listing advantages to consolidate the new belief
1149.skill_description: Summarize the new viewpoints formed in the dialogue, compare them item by item with the old beliefs and mark the key evidence and change points; invite orally listing and writing down at least 5 of one's own strengths and resources, combined with orally contrasting the old negative statements with positive self-suggestion, promote a dialogue between new and old beliefs, strengthen the degree of belief and self-efficacy and transfer them to similar situations.
1149.when_to_use: At the stage of dialogue closure and consolidation, or when self-evaluation is low and self-deprecation repeated, and concrete self-talk needs to be specified and the new belief started and internalized.
1149.trigger: The client shows agreement with the new viewpoint such as 'it seems so / pretty good' and emotional relief; or repeatedly has negative self-talk, has difficulty seeing strengths, and has low acceptance of the new viewpoint.

1074.skill_name: Dispute old beliefs and generate reasonable alternatives
1074.skill_description: Using debate techniques, guide listing old and constructive beliefs in pairs or placing before/after beliefs side by side, questioning the basis and logic of each item, recording old beliefs and responding with counterexamples, comparing the basis, consequences and applicable situations of each pair of beliefs, generating specific rational statements, so that rational beliefs gradually replace the original irrational ideas, reducing Anxiety and pessimistic emotions.
1074.when_to_use: In the new-old belief dialogue segment or the working-through, re-education consolidation phase, when irrational beliefs have been identified and need challenging, substitution and consolidation; or when strong emotions accompany irrational beliefs.
1074.trigger: Acknowledging old beliefs are problematic but still troubled; expressing absolute beliefs like 'must/certainly' with anger, Anxiety or depression; insisting on statements like 'no hope for the future' or uncertain about the evidence basis, seeking answers.

906.skill_name: Review homework and progress and reinforce rational beliefs
906.skill_description: In subsequent sessions, systematically review the process and effects of homework and behavioral attempts, review and consolidate new cognitive methods and rational ideas, highlighting successful experiences and giving clear affirmation and reinforcement feedback; guide summarizing counseling gains, connecting new understanding with specific life scenarios, fine-tuning homework arrangements when necessary, improving substitution and maintenance of irrational beliefs.
906.when_to_use: At the start or end of each session, during the Consolidation and termination phase, for checking homework, consolidating gains and planning next steps.
906.trigger: The client brings record forms, gives feedback on practice experience, or reports difficulties and improvements; emotional improvement exists but needs further consolidation and integration.

960.skill_name: Train and use positive self-talk and self-suggestion
960.skill_description: Encourage using positive self-talk/self-suggestion in daily situations to counter irrational cognitions, targeting automated thoughts like 'looks down on me', 'not a member of the class', 'hate myself', practicing more rational, constructive alternative statements; simultaneously doing thought records and self-affirmation lists, positive focus exercises, enhancing confidence, weakening inferiority and depressive Interpretations, reducing Anxiety and consolidating new ideas.
960.when_to_use: The stage of consolidating cognitive change and preventing relapse, as homework and daily practice; when emotions fluctuate or setbacks are encountered in daily life.
960.trigger: When thoughts of being looked down upon or excluded appear, or Self-blame emotions are low; when frustrated in study, relationships or worried about exam prospects.

1138.skill_name: Review progress and reinforce self-help application
1138.skill_description: In the termination/consolidation phase, systematically review key progress and practice insights from previous sessions, Inviting the client to restate counseling key points, specifically affirming effort and effectiveness, sorting and summarizing effective strategies and caveats, enhancing self-efficacy and willingness to use, preparing for daily self-help application and follow-up.
1138.when_to_use: Consolidation review before the stage or termination, ending and consolidation sessions, late treatment stage.
1138.trigger: When needing to integrate gains after multiple practices; entering the last session or phased summary, the client asks about effectiveness or expresses uncertainty.

1173.skill_name: Summarize coping strategies and develop relapse prevention
1173.skill_description: Jointly summarize with the client the causes of symptom/Fear occurrence and maintenance, generalize methods that have worked, clarify coping steps for future recurrence and key points for identifying relapse signs, forming a checklist for easy review and self-reminding, to consolidate skills and prevent relapse.
1173.when_to_use: At stage consolidation or near the end, or when a long-term self-help plan needs to be formed and subsequent self-help strategies formulated.
1173.trigger: Symptoms clearly improve, preparing to reduce session frequency or nearing the end; the client worries about maintaining change and relapse risk.

837.skill_name: Assign and review automatic-thought recording practice
837.skill_description: Teach how to fill in thought/ABC records, and assign homework fitting the session's theme at the end of each session; require recording event–thought–emotion–behavior and alternative views in daily situations, covering multiple similar situations, forming continuous materials; review insights and gains in the next session, consolidating identification, assessment and application of rational beliefs.
837.when_to_use: After automatic-thought work begins, at the consolidation stage at the end of each session; reviewing homework at the start of the next session.
837.trigger: The client is willing to practice and record in life, bringing concrete events and feelings, or needs to transfer what was learned to daily situations.

912.skill_name: Review, summarize, and teach emotion-regulation strategies
912.skill_description: In the consolidation phase, Reviewing the counseling process and belief changes, affirming progress, and teaching scientific emotional venting and help-seeking strategies; combining learned thought identification, time planning, behavioral verification and other methods, clarifying transfer practices in study and life, supporting long-term maintenance and self-help.
912.when_to_use: In the late and closing stages of counseling, used to integrate gains, plan subsequent self-management, and prevent relapse.
912.trigger: Counseling is nearing its end and a maintenance plan needs to be formulated and self-regulation ability strengthened; the client worries about maintaining effects or needs a clear path for subsequent application.

887.skill_name: Map support resources and develop a self-help plan
887.skill_description: Jointly list personal and environmental resources with the client, systematically summarizing 'friend and family support' and the 'psychological resilience and strengths' shown in counseling, and developing follow-up Self-exploration and resource support plans at termination, enhancing self-regulation and independent coping, reducing dependence on counseling.
887.when_to_use: In the consolidation stage and case-closing segment, when self-help capacity and resource mobilization need to be enhanced and the follow-up path arranged.
887.trigger: The client has concerns about relapse prevention, or is willing to keep moving forward and needs resource support, when entering the summary and feedback stage.

1161.skill_name: Guide and assign daily relaxation training practice
1161.skill_description: Teach and assign Relaxation training, so the client repeatedly practices in daily life to reduce tension and Anxiety; consolidate and generalize in real situations based on the hierarchy table/session content, recording practice effects when necessary, supporting the application of new cognitions and the maintenance of Emotion management.
1161.when_to_use: At the session consolidation stage and after completing a training, when the relaxation technique needs to be transferred to daily situations and the emotion regulation ability consolidated.
1161.trigger: When the client reports high Anxiety factors, rising study pressure, difficulty concentrating or frequent tense situations in life.

1148.skill_name: Scheduling daily relaxation practice and recording
1148.skill_description: Arrange fixed daily or as-needed breathing/muscle relaxation practice, cooperating with emotion dialogue when necessary; apply promptly when tension, insomnia, palpitations occur, and record changes and subjective feelings after practice, to consolidate skills and improve self-regulation in real situations.
1148.when_to_use: During the consolidation phase and between sessions, to prevent emotional recurrence, increase skill automation, or when Anxiety physiological reactions are obvious.
1148.trigger: When psychosomatic reactions like restless unease, tension, Difficulty falling asleep, inattention, chest tightness and palpitations occur, or practice effects need tracking.

953.skill_name: Create a relapse-prevention checklist and coping cards
953.skill_description: Together with the client, draft a relapse early-warning and coping checklist stating high-risk situations, signs of relapse, immediate self-prompts and executable steps, list available tools and support resources, make a pocket coping card, and encourage continued review of homework, so as to apply it in daily life and maintain and consolidate the treatment effect.
953.when_to_use: Before closing or in the late stage of treatment, to transfer to daily life and maintain outcomes and implement the prevention plan.
953.trigger: Core symptoms are relieved, preparing to end counseling; the client or parents worry about relapse, or signs of problem recurrence appear.

952.skill_name: Daily practice of self-disputation and rational statements
952.skill_description: Aiming at the irrational/absolutist thoughts that pop up, continuously carry out self-disputation, distinguish evidence from inference, propose counter-evidence and generate rational self-statements; one may adopt daily or weekly written practice and disputing at any time, repeatedly read aloud and internalize, to consolidate the new cognitions and lower the possibility of the old patterns rekindling.
952.when_to_use: Used in the later stage of psychological help through to the consolidation stage, in session gaps and at phased summaries, to maintain and generalize cognitive restructuring outcomes.
952.trigger: Automatic thoughts of self-blame, catastrophizing, excessive worry, avoidance tendencies or self-deprecation appear; at the end-of-day review or when willing to carry out self-help practice.

1165.skill_name: Teach breathing and muscle relaxation and apply in situations
1165.skill_description: Teach diaphragmatic breathing and progressive muscle relaxation, require practicing before bed and when anxious, and applying when stress is high, insomnia or attention is unfocused, to relieve physiological tension, improve sleep, forming situational self-help strategies, supporting the application of cognitive adjustment.
1165.when_to_use: When Difficulty falling asleep exists, Anxiety physiological reactions intensify or functioning is affected, self-regulation training and daily application are needed.
1165.trigger: When tension signals like Difficulty falling asleep, waking easily, palpitations, bodily tension, inability to concentrate appear.

1085.skill_name: Aggregate across situations and summarize common themes of automatic thoughts
1085.skill_description: Collect and organize automatic thought/emotion/behavior records from multiple situations (three-column forms, thought record books, etc.), horizontally compare the high-frequency wording and reaction patterns, classify them by dimensions such as ability, self-worth, being accepted/being loved, distill the repeatedly appearing common core, as a basis for core-belief candidates.
1085.when_to_use: After completing several records or multiple sessions, entering case conceptualization or cross-sectional case analysis, when deeper themes need to be induced from multi-situation material.
1085.trigger: When similar self-blame, insufficient ability, not being liked/excluded expressions frequently appear across situations, accompanied by stable negative emotions or similar reaction patterns; multiple records point to the same evaluation theme.

984.skill_name: Naming common themes as core beliefs and verifying
984.skill_description: After inducing cross-situational commonalities, summarize them into concise core belief wording (such as 'worthless', 'incompetent', 'not liked/unlovable'), present them in dialogue and check fit with the client, forming preliminary consensus on core beliefs, incorporating into conceptualization.
984.when_to_use: Used after completing cross-situational comparison and stable repeated themes have appeared, preparing to enter core / intermediate belief work and before revision.
984.trigger: The same theme words or judgments appear with high frequency across multiple records, with high belief or strong emotions; the client resonates with general statements or shows obvious emotional reactions.

882.skill_name: Review homework and summarize recurring cross-situational themes
882.skill_description: In the session, collect and sort ABC/thought record homework, comparing Automatic thoughts and emotional reactions across different entries, categorizing by ability, being accepted, self-worth and other dimensions, capturing recurring themes, providing a basis for distilling core beliefs.
882.when_to_use: When the client has completed record homework, needing to integrate materials in session and identify the common core of core beliefs; or during the generalization segment of the second to third phase.
882.trigger: When multiple comparable records appear in session; Automatic thoughts under different events keep revolving around similar evaluations like 'useless/write badly/excluded' with high emotion ratings.

957.skill_name: Name the core belief and incorporate it into cognitive conceptualization
957.skill_description: Directly distill the induced recurring themes into core belief categories (such as 'incompetent', 'unlovable', 'world unsafe'), and check consistency with specific examples and current distress, forming cognitive conceptualization conclusions, guiding subsequent Intervention.
957.when_to_use: After completing the Automatic thoughts theme induction, when core beliefs need to be clarified and used to set Intervention goals or enter subsequent assessment.
957.trigger: When stable themes of ability and self-worth/being recognized have been identified, and the client's social setbacks, avoidance or lowness are highly related to them.

1045.skill_name: Collect and compare automatic thoughts across situations to summarize the core
1045.skill_description: List Automatic thoughts and emotion-behavior clues from multiple daily/social scenarios (three-column table, etc.), horizontally comparing their commonalities and negative hypotheses (such as being scrutinized, being negated, insufficient ability, 'must/should'), summarizing recurring common cores, providing a basis for subsequent restructuring.
